In-scope processes.value: Major incident lifecycle for the broker-dealer and its variable annuity platform: Sev-1/Sev-2 declaration, containment, customer-impact scoping, Rule 4530 reportability assessment, FINRA Gateway filing, BCP/emergency-contact refresh and post-incident review

In-scope systems.value: Sev-1/Sev-2 incident records and timestamps in ServiceNow ITSM feed the 30-day clock; detection evidence comes from the SIEM and filings are made in FINRA Gateway

Compliance procedure documented.value: Regulatory Incident Reporting Procedure (WSP section 4530/4370) — severity triggers, the 4530(a)/(b) decision tree, who files, what Part I/II fields are completed, and the Reg S-P 30-day customer notification path

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved jointly by the Head of Compliance and the Chief Risk Officer; re-approved annually and re-opened after every Sev-1 or any FINRA late-filing finding

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Rule 4530(a) events and 4530(b) self-identified violations: 30 calendar days from the date the firm knows or should have known; Rule 4530(f) copies of complaints/arbitrations: 10 business days; Reg S-P customer notification: 30 days from determining unauthorised access; Rule 4370(e) emergency contact updates: promptly, with an annual review

Deadline reminders configured.value: The incident record opens a 4530 clock task at declaration with automated reminders at day 5 (assessment due), day 15 (draft filing due) and day 25 (escalation to Head of Compliance if unfiled)

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs every 'not reportable' conclusion and every late-filing remediation before the incident record is closed

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly 4530 incident-reporting workpaper (population extract, clock recomputation, filing confirmations, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under FINRA/4530

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Incident register export, per-incident timeline with detection and determination timestamps, and the FINRA Gateway 4530 filing confirmations, assembled for a FINRA examination request within 5 business days

checklist.step: Declare the incident and start the regulatory clock
actions: In ServiceNow open the incident record and set Severity to Sev-1 or Sev-2, Category to 'Operational/ICT', and the Business Service to the affected platform (order entry, variable annuity administration, customer portal).

Record the detection timestamp from the SOC alert and the declaration timestamp separately — the 30-calendar-day Rule 4530 clock is measured from when the firm knew or should have known, not from declaration.
Add the Operational Risk Manager and the Compliance Officer as watchers on the record so the reportability assessment task is created automatically.
Attach the initial paging/bridge log so the timeline is reconstructable later.
checklist.done: the incident record carries a severity, a detection timestamp, a declaration timestamp and an open 4530 assessment task.

checklist.step: Pull the detection evidence out of the SIEM and fix the impact window
actions: Run the incident correlation search in Splunk over the affected indexes and export the first and last event timestamps that bound the impact window.
Identify the systems and data stores touched and state plainly whether customer account records or non-public personal information were reachable.
Hand the exported event set and the impact window to the Operational Risk Manager as the factual basis for the reportability memo.
Attach the search string and export to the incident record so the analysis can be re-run.
checklist.done: the impact window, affected systems and any customer-data exposure are documented from SIEM evidence and attached to the incident.

checklist.step: Scope customer and account impact with the servicing teams
actions: Query the policy administration platform for contracts and accounts transacting inside the impact window and count those with failed, delayed or duplicated transactions.
Ask the Contact Center Ops Manager for the call and complaint volume attributable to the outage and record it against the incident.
Produce a numbered impact schedule: accounts affected, transactions affected, dollar value at risk, and whether any customer suffered financial harm.
Send the schedule to the Operational Risk Manager and the Compliance Officer the same business day.
checklist.done: a numbered customer-impact schedule with account counts, transaction counts and dollar value is attached to the incident.

checklist.step: Run the Rule 4530 reportability decision tree
actions: Open the WSP 4530 decision tree and walk each 4530(a)(1)(A) trigger in turn: violation of securities laws or FINRA rules, statutory disqualification, customer complaint involving theft or forgery, regulatory or SRO action.

Separately apply Rule 4530(b): has the firm concluded, or reasonably should have concluded, that it or an associated person violated a rule — an outage that prevented required order handling or timely confirmation delivery usually does.
Record the exact date the firm 'knew or should have known' and compute the day-30 due date from it, not from the remediation date.
Write a reportability memo stating the trigger relied on (or the reason none applies) with the rule text quoted.
checklist.done: a dated reportability memo names the applicable 4530 trigger or the reason none applies, and states the computed day-30 due date.

checklist.step: Get Regulatory Counsel to clear the reportability call
actions: Read the reportability memo against the current text of Rule 4530 and Supplementary Material .01 (meaning of 'conclusion of a violation') and .08 (reporting by associated persons).
Confirm or overturn the call in writing on the memo, and where the call is 'not reportable' state the specific fact that takes the event outside the rule.
Where the incident exposed non-public personal information, open the parallel Reg S-P assessment and its own 30-day customer-notification clock.
Return the cleared memo to Operational Risk no later than day 10 so there is filing time left.
checklist.done: counsel has confirmed or overturned the reportability call in writing, dated, with the Reg S-P path opened where data was exposed.

checklist.step: Draft the FINRA Rule 4530 filing in FINRA Gateway
actions: Log in to FINRA Gateway with your entitled user id and open the Rule 4530 Reporting application (Regulatory Filings menu).

Start a new 4530 disclosure, select the Problem Code that matches the event (for an ICT outage affecting order handling, the operational/systems code) and enter the event date and the date of the firm's conclusion.
Complete the narrative fields with the impact window, accounts and transactions affected, root cause as then understood, and the remedial steps taken and planned.
Attach the impact schedule and, where the event arose from a customer complaint or litigation, the underlying document.
checklist.done: a complete 4530 disclosure sits in FINRA Gateway with problem code, dates, narrative and attachments ready for review.

checklist.step: Review and submit the filing before day 30
actions: Compare the narrative against the incident timeline and the counsel memo; correct any date that does not match the ServiceNow record.
Confirm the submission date is on or before the computed day-30 due date and, if it is not, note the reason for lateness in the filing itself rather than concealing it.
Submit in FINRA Gateway and download the submission confirmation with its filing reference number.
Paste the filing reference and submission timestamp onto the incident record and close the 4530 clock task.
checklist.done: the 4530 filing is submitted within 30 calendar days and the confirmation reference is recorded on the incident.

checklist.step: File Rule 4530(f) copies where litigation or arbitration follows
actions: Ask Litigation Counsel for any civil complaint, arbitration claim or criminal indictment served on the firm or an associated person arising from the incident.
File the copy through FINRA Gateway Rule 4530 Reporting within 10 business days of the firm's receipt of service — this deadline is separate from and shorter than the 30-day event clock.
Log the service date, the filing date and the day count on the 4530 register so the 10-business-day maths is auditable.
Set a recurring check with Litigation Counsel for late-arriving claims tied to the same incident.
checklist.done: every complaint or arbitration arising from the incident is filed within 10 business days with the day count recorded.

checklist.step: Refresh Rule 4370 emergency contact information and the BCP entry
actions: In FINRA Gateway open the FINRA Contact System and confirm the two emergency contacts (one a member of senior management, both registered principals) are current, with mobile numbers reachable when the primary site is down.
Update any contact changed by the incident response and record the update date — Rule 4370(f) requires prompt update and an annual review.
Add the incident's failure mode to the Business Continuity Plan under the affected business function and revise the recovery time objective if it was missed.
Circulate the revised BCP section to the Chief Risk Officer for acceptance.
checklist.done: FINRA emergency contacts are verified current and the BCP section for the failed function is updated and accepted.

checklist.step: Notify customers where non-public personal information was accessed
actions: Apply the Reg S-P standard: notify affected individuals as soon as practicable and no later than 30 days after becoming aware that unauthorised access to sensitive customer information has occurred or is reasonably likely.
Draft the notice covering what happened, the data elements involved, the date range, what the firm has done, and the contact route for questions, and have Regulatory Counsel clear it.
Produce the notification population from the impact schedule, reconcile the count to the mailing file, and retain the mail-house confirmation.
Record the awareness date, the mailing date and the day count on the incident record.
checklist.done: affected customers are notified within 30 days of the awareness date, with the population reconciled and the day count recorded.

checklist.step: Log the operational risk event and the loss
actions: Create an operational risk event record linked to the ServiceNow incident number, classified by Basel-style event type (business disruption and system failure, or execution/delivery failure).
Enter the gross loss: customer remediation payments, trade-correction losses, vendor costs and regulatory fees, with the general ledger account each was booked to.
Link the event to the affected risk and control in the risk register and mark the control as failed where it did not detect or prevent the incident.
Ask the Controller to confirm the booked loss figures in writing before the record is finalised.
checklist.done: an operational risk event exists with a classified event type, GL-confirmed loss figures and links to the failed control.

checklist.step: Hold the post-incident review and agree corrective actions
actions: Chair the review within 10 business days of service restoration with Incident Response, the platform owner, Compliance and the affected business line.
Establish root cause using the timeline and the SIEM evidence rather than the first plausible explanation, and state which control failed.
Raise each corrective action as a tracked item with a named owner and a due date, separating tactical fixes from the design change that prevents recurrence.
Record whether the recovery time objective and recovery point objective in the BCP were met.
checklist.done: a written post-incident review states root cause, the failed control, RTO/RPO performance and owned corrective actions with due dates.

checklist.step: Report the incident and the filing into governance
actions: Add the incident to the quarterly Operational Risk and Compliance report to the Risk Committee with the 4530 filing reference and the day count achieved.
Flag any incident that missed the 30-day clock as a standing item until the underlying process is fixed.
Give the Corporate Secretary the summary for the board pack and confirm the minute records the committee's acceptance.
Carry unresolved corrective actions forward on the committee's open-items schedule.
checklist.done: the incident, its filing reference and its corrective actions are minuted at the Risk Committee.

checklist.step: Update the WSPs and retrain where the procedure itself failed
actions: Where the reportability call was slow or wrong, amend the WSP 4530 section: sharpen the trigger definitions, name the decider, and shorten the internal assessment deadline.
Version the WSP, capture the Head of Compliance approval date, and publish the superseded version to the archive rather than overwriting it.
Assign a short refresher to Operational Risk, the SOC and the incident commanders in the learning management system with a completion deadline.
Track completion and chase non-completers at 14 days.
checklist.done: the WSP is versioned and approved, and the refresher is assigned with completion tracked.

checklist.step: File the incident evidence for the retention period
actions: Move the incident pack — timeline, SIEM export, impact schedule, reportability memo, counsel clearance, 4530 confirmation, customer notices, post-incident review — into the compliance evidence repository under FINRA/4530/<year>/<incident id>.
Apply the six-year retention label with the first two years in an easily accessible place, per SEA Rule 17a-4(b).
Confirm the pack is indexed and retrievable by incident id, filing reference and event date.
Record the archive location on the ServiceNow incident before closing it.
checklist.done: the incident pack is archived under a six-year retention label and retrievable by incident id and filing reference.

testing.step: Build the population of reportable-candidate events for the quarter
actions: Extract from ServiceNow every incident with Severity Sev-1 or Sev-2 and every incident tagged 'Operational/ICT' with a customer-impact flag, for the quarter, with detection and declaration timestamps.
Add the Rule 4530(a) trigger events held outside ServiceNow: regulatory actions received, statutory disqualification events, and complaints alleging theft, forgery or misappropriation.
Add every civil complaint and arbitration served in the quarter from Litigation Counsel's matter list, since those carry the separate 10-business-day 4530(f) clock.
testing.done: the population combines incident, complaint and litigation sources and its counts are signed as complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the SOC and change records
actions: Compare the incident population to the SIEM's major-alert log and the change management failed-change list for the same dates.
Investigate any major alert or failed change with customer impact that never became an incident record — under-declaration is the most common way the clock never starts.
Resolve every difference in writing with the SOC Lead and the Change Coordinator before sampling.
testing.done: the incident population reconciles to SIEM major alerts and failed changes, with all differences explained in writing.

testing.step: Draw the sample and document the method
actions: Take 100% of Sev-1 incidents and 100% of 4530(f) litigation items — these carry the highest filing risk.
Take 20 Sev-2 incidents by seeded random selection from the remainder, minimum 30 items overall.
Record the seed, population size, selection date and any items excluded with the reason, so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all Sev-1 and all 4530(f) items is documented with its seed and population size.

testing.step: Re-perform the reportability decision independently
actions: For each sampled item, read the incident timeline and impact schedule and reach your own Rule 4530(a)/(b) conclusion before opening the reportability memo.
Compare your conclusion to the recorded one; a correct outcome supported by the wrong trigger or an unstated 'knew or should have known' date is still an exception.
For 'not reportable' calls, confirm the memo names the specific fact that takes it outside the rule and carries a dated counsel clearance.
Capture the rule text you relied on, dated, into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled item has an independent reportability conclusion recorded against the firm's conclusion.

testing.step: Recompute the 30-day and 10-business-day clocks
actions: For each filed item, recompute day-30 as the 'knew or should have known' date plus 30 calendar days, and compare it to the FINRA Gateway submission timestamp.
For 4530(f) items, recompute the 10-business-day due date from the service date using the firm's business-day calendar including exchange holidays.
Challenge any 'knew or should have known' date later than the SIEM detection timestamp or the complaint receipt stamp — a shifted start date is a common way a late filing is made to look timely.
List every item filed on or after day 31 as a fail regardless of remediation.
testing.done: every clock is recomputed from source timestamps and each late filing is listed as a fail.

testing.step: Trace filings to FINRA Gateway confirmations
actions: In FINRA Gateway open Rule 4530 Reporting and list the firm's submissions for the quarter with their filing references and submission dates.
Match each sampled reportable item to a submission on problem code, event date and narrative subject; flag any item with no matching submission.
Check the reverse direction as well: any Gateway submission with no incident record behind it indicates events being handled outside the procedure.
Screenshot each matched submission detail screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled reportable item traces to a FINRA Gateway submission, and unmatched submissions are investigated.

testing.step: Test the Reg S-P customer notification population
actions: For incidents involving non-public personal information, recompute notification due date as awareness date plus 30 days and compare it to the mailing date.
Reconcile the notified population to the impact schedule account list and explain any account dropped between the two.
Read one sample notice and confirm it states the data elements involved, the date range and the firm's remedial steps.
testing.done: notifications reconcile to the impact schedule, were mailed within 30 days, and the notice content is verified.

testing.step: Verify the Rule 4370 emergency contact and BCP updates
actions: In FINRA Gateway open the FINRA Contact System and confirm two current emergency contacts are recorded, at least one a member of senior management, both registered principals.
Compare the recorded contacts to the current organisation chart and confirm the last review date is inside the last twelve months.
Confirm the BCP section for each sampled Sev-1's business function was updated after the incident and that the RTO was revised where it was missed.
testing.done: emergency contacts are current and reviewed within twelve months, and post-incident BCP updates are evidenced.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one issue per exception carrying the incident id, the clock missed, the day count and the customer impact.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list — under-declared severity, shifted start date, counsel clearance bottleneck, no owner while on leave — and name an accountable owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any unfiled reportable event, open a late 4530 filing immediately rather than waiting for remediation.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the on-time filing rate and compare it to the zero-late-filing threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references supporting it.
Have the Internal Auditor, who owns no sampled reportability memo, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report the conclusion and any unfiled events to the Risk Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the on-time filing rate, a conclusion and the committee reporting date.

checklist.step: Sweep FINRA's published notices and open a change record for each
actions: Every Monday review FINRA's Regulatory Notices and Rule Filings pages plus the SEC Federal Register approval orders for the prior week.
For each item open a regulatory change record capturing notice number, publication date, rule numbers touched, effective date and comment-period deadline.
Attach the notice PDF and the marked-up rule text to the record so later readers see the version as published.
Set the determination due date at publication date plus 30 days.
checklist.done: every FINRA notice from the week has a change record with notice number, rule numbers, effective date and a 30-day determination due date.

checklist.step: Decompose the notice into atomic, testable obligations
actions: Read the rule text sentence by sentence and write one obligation row for each distinct 'must', 'shall' or prohibition — do not carry a whole rule as one obligation.
For Rule 1240(b) that yields separate rows for the annual needs analysis, the written training plan, the delivery to covered registered persons, and the record of completion.
For each row record the trigger (annual, per communication, per recommendation), the actor, the artifact produced and the pass condition.
Quote the operative sentence verbatim on the row so the obligation cannot drift from the text.
checklist.done: each notice is broken into numbered obligation rows, each with a quoted operative sentence, trigger, actor, artifact and pass condition.

checklist.step: Test applicability against the firm's products and registered population
actions: For each obligation row, test applicability against the firm's business: variable annuities and variable life distributed through the broker-dealer, the registered representative population by registration category, and the retail versus institutional customer mix.
Get the registered-person counts by Series category from the Producer Licensing Coordinator so 'covered registered persons' under Rule 1240(b) is a number, not an assertion.
Where an obligation does not apply, name the specific exclusion in the rule text that makes it inapplicable — never record a bare 'N/A'.
Where applicability turns on a threshold, record the tested value and its source.
checklist.done: every obligation row is marked applicable or not applicable with a quoted basis and, where relevant, a counted population.

checklist.step: Map each applicable obligation to the WSP section that carries it
actions: Open the written supervisory procedures and locate the section that already addresses the obligation; record the section number on the obligation row.
Where no section exists, mark the row 'WSP gap' and raise a drafting task on the Compliance Analyst with a due date inside the notice's effective date.
Where a section exists but predates the amendment, mark it 'WSP amendment required' and attach the sentence needing change.
Confirm the mapping covers supervision as well as performance — Rule 3110(b) requires a procedure for supervising the activity, not just doing it.
checklist.done: every applicable obligation points to a WSP section, or carries a dated gap or amendment task.

checklist.step: Assign a single accountable owner and get written acceptance
actions: Assign each applicable obligation to one named individual by role — Firm Element delivery to the Learning Development Manager, communications approval to the Marketing Compliance Analyst, registration maintenance to the Producer Compliance Manager.
Send the obligation row to the proposed owner and require a written acceptance recording that they can see the work, the frequency and the evidence expected.
Where an owner declines, arbitrate within five business days rather than leaving the row unowned.
Record the acceptance date and the owner's supervisor on the row.
checklist.done: every applicable obligation carries one named owner with a dated written acceptance.

checklist.step: Set the frequency, deadline and evidence artifact on each row
actions: Record the obligation frequency exactly as the rule sets it: Firm Element needs analysis annually with delivery closing by December 31; retail communication approval before the earlier of use or filing; principal review within 10 business days where the rule sets one.
Name the evidence artifact that will prove performance — needs-analysis memo, approved training plan, learning management system completion extract, principal approval stamp.
State the retention period against each artifact using SEA Rule 17a-4 as the baseline.
Load the deadline into the compliance calendar with the owner as the assignee.
checklist.done: every row states a frequency, a hard deadline, a named evidence artifact and a retention period, and appears in the compliance calendar.

checklist.step: Run the annual Firm Element needs analysis that Rule 1240(b) requires
actions: Assemble the inputs: the prior year's customer complaints, internal inspection and Rule 3120 findings, disciplinary history, new products launched, and FINRA examination priorities.
Map the findings to the covered registered persons who sell variable annuities and variable life and identify the specific knowledge gaps.
Write the needs analysis memo naming each identified training need, the population it applies to and the evidence that raised it.
Date and sign the memo before the training plan is drafted — the analysis must precede the plan, not rationalise it.
checklist.done: a dated needs-analysis memo links each training need to named source evidence and a defined covered population.

checklist.step: Approve the written Firm Element training plan
actions: Draft the written training plan mapping each need from the analysis to a module, a delivery method, a covered population and a completion deadline before 31 December.
Include the product-specific content Rule 1240(b) requires — variable annuity features, surrender charges, living benefit riders, exchange analysis, and the applicable regulatory developments.
Route the plan to the Head of Compliance for written approval and record the approval date.
Publish the plan to the learning management system catalogue so assignment can begin.
checklist.done: an approved written training plan links every identified need to a module, population and pre-31-December deadline.

checklist.step: Confirm content standards obligations reach the communications owners
actions: Extract the Rule 2210(d)(1) obligations — fair and balanced, sound basis for evaluation, no false or exaggerated statements, no predictions of performance, prominent firm name — as separate reviewer checklist lines.
Add the Rule 2211 requirements specific to variable life and variable annuity communications, including the treatment of hypothetical illustrations and guarantees.
Hand the checklist lines to the communications reviewers and confirm the review tool now blocks approval when a line is unanswered.
Record the checklist version and effective date on the obligation row.
checklist.done: content-standards obligations exist as enforced reviewer checklist lines with a versioned effective date.

checklist.step: Register the obligations and publish the register
actions: Load each obligation row into the GRC obligation register with rule cite, quoted text, applicability, owner, frequency, deadline, evidence artifact and WSP section.
Link each register row to its control and to the notice record it came from so the chain from notice to control is unbroken.
Publish a read-only register view to the business owners and to Internal Audit.
Set the register row status to Active only once the owner acceptance and WSP mapping are both present.
checklist.done: the register holds one complete, source-linked row per obligation with no Active row missing an owner or WSP link.

checklist.step: Escalate contested applicability and unowned obligations
actions: Review every obligation marked not applicable and every row unowned after ten business days.
Re-read the cited rule text and either confirm the exclusion in writing on the row or overturn it and force an owner assignment.
Where the answer genuinely turns on FINRA's view, submit an interpretive question through FINRA's Regulatory Interpretation request route and log the question, date and response on the row.
Report unresolved rows to the Head of Compliance weekly until cleared.
checklist.done: no obligation is left not-applicable or unowned without a dated counsel decision or a logged FINRA interpretive request.

checklist.step: Brief the business owners on what changed and when it bites
actions: Hold a change briefing with Distribution, Marketing, Producer Licensing and Operations covering each applicable obligation, its effective date and what will visibly change in their process.
Give each owner the evidence artifact specification so they build the record as they work rather than reconstructing it at test time.
Confirm each owner's supervisor knows their team carries the obligation, since Rule 3110 makes supervision the firm's obligation too.
Circulate the briefing note and record attendance.
checklist.done: every owner and their supervisor has been briefed, with attendance recorded and the evidence specification issued.

checklist.step: Fold the determinations into the annual Rule 3130 certification pack
actions: Extract the year's determinations and register additions into the Rule 3130 report supporting the chief executive's annual certification.
Note any obligation still without a completed WSP amendment as an open item in the report rather than omitting it.
Meet the Chief Executive Officer to walk the report, and record the meeting date as the rule requires.
File the signed certification and its supporting report.
checklist.done: the year's determinations appear in the Rule 3130 report and the certification meeting is dated and recorded.

checklist.step: Re-validate the register against the live Rulebook annually
actions: Take each Active register row and re-open the cited rule in the FINRA Rulebook to confirm the quoted sentence still reads the same and the rule has not been renumbered or deleted.
Flag any row whose quoted text no longer matches for immediate re-determination.
Confirm each owner is still in post by checking the roster with HR, and reassign vacant rows the same week.
Record the re-validation date and the reviewer on every row.
checklist.done: every Active row shows a current-year re-validation date, a matching quoted text and an in-post owner.

checklist.step: Archive the determination evidence
actions: Move each determination pack — notice PDF, decomposition sheet, applicability analysis, owner acceptances, counsel clearances — into the compliance evidence repository under FINRA/determinations/<year>/<notice number>.
Apply the six-year retention label and confirm the pack indexes by notice number, rule number and owner.
Link the archive location back onto the GRC change record.
Confirm superseded determinations remain retrievable rather than being overwritten by the current version.
checklist.done: every determination pack is archived under six-year retention and retrievable by notice number and rule number.

testing.step: Build the population of FINRA notices published in the period
actions: Take FINRA's published Regulatory Notices list and rule-filing log for the quarter directly from finra.org rather than from the firm's intake list.
Add SEC approval orders for FINRA rule changes published in the Federal Register in the same period.
Record the count and the source date so the population is reproducible.
testing.done: an independently sourced list of the period's FINRA notices and approval orders exists with a recorded count.

testing.step: Reconcile the regulator's list to the firm's intake register
actions: Match each notice on the regulator's list to a GRC regulatory change record on notice number.
List every notice with no change record — a missing intake means the obligation was never assessed at all.
Check the reverse for change records citing notices that do not exist or were withdrawn.
Agree the reconciliation with the Regulatory Affairs Manager before sampling.
testing.done: every published notice is matched to an intake record or listed as a completeness exception.

testing.step: Draw the sample of determinations to re-perform
actions: Take 100% of notices touching Rules 1240, 2210, 2211, 2111 and 3110, since those drive the firm's variable-product distribution.
Take 10 further notices by seeded random selection from the remainder.
Record the seed, the population size and the selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all variable-product-relevant notices is documented with its seed.

testing.step: Re-perform the decomposition on the sample
actions: Read the rule text for each sampled notice and write your own list of atomic obligations before opening the firm's decomposition sheet.
Compare counts and content; an obligation the firm rolled into another row, or omitted entirely, is an exception.
Confirm each firm row quotes the operative sentence and that the quote matches the current Rulebook text.
Capture the Rulebook page, dated, into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled notice has an independent obligation list compared line by line against the firm's.

testing.step: Challenge the applicability calls
actions: Pull every row marked not applicable in the sample and read the exclusion the firm relied on in the rule text as it read on the determination date.
Confirm the exclusion covers the firm's actual business, testing it against the product list and the registered-person counts rather than accepting the assertion.
Treat a bare 'N/A' with no quoted exclusion as a fail, not a documentation gap.
Record a written concurrence or challenge against each row.
testing.done: every not-applicable row carries a counsel concurrence or is raised as a failed determination.

testing.step: Recompute the determination and implementation day counts
actions: For each sampled notice recompute determination due date as publication date plus 30 days and implementation-plan due date as publication plus 60 days.
Compare to the memo sign-off dates in the GRC record and list every overrun with its day count.
Separately confirm the Firm Element needs analysis was signed before the training plan was approved, and that the plan's completion deadlines all fall on or before 31 December.
Flag any deadline recorded later than the rule's own effective date.
testing.done: every determination and implementation day count is recomputed and each overrun is listed with its size.

testing.step: Test ownership coverage across the whole register
actions: Export every Active obligation row and filter for rows with no owner, no acceptance date, or an owner no longer on the HR roster.
Sample 15 owned rows and obtain the written acceptance from the owner's mailbox or the GRC audit trail.
Confirm each row also carries a WSP section reference and that the referenced section exists in the current WSP version.
testing.done: no Active row lacks an in-post owner, a dated acceptance or a valid WSP reference, or the gap is logged.

testing.step: Trace two obligations end to end into live evidence
actions: Take the Rule 1240(b) Firm Element obligation and trace notice, determination, owner, training plan, and completion extract from the learning management system for the covered population.
Take a Rule 2210(d)(1) content-standards obligation and trace to the reviewer checklist actually used on a recent retail communication.
Confirm the evidence artifact produced is the one the register named, not a substitute reconstructed for the test.
testing.done: two obligations trace unbroken from published notice to live evidence produced in the ordinary course.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception recording the notice number, the obligation, what was missed and the exposure if a FINRA examination hit it today.
Assign a root cause — notice not intaken, decomposition too coarse, applicability asserted without a cite, owner never accepted — and a named owner.
Set a remediation date inside 30 days for missing determinations and inside 10 business days for unowned applicable obligations.
Carry open exceptions into the next quarter's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute intake completeness, on-time determination rate and ownership coverage against the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper sections behind each number.
Have the Internal Auditor, who authored no sampled determination, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report to the Compliance Committee and fold unresolved items into the Rule 3130 report.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the three rates, a conclusion and the committee reporting date.

checklist.step: Derive the covered registered person population from CRD
actions: In FINRA Gateway open the CRD registration reports and export the firm's registered persons with registration categories, branch codes and supervisory flags.
Apply the Rule 1240(b) definition of covered registered persons — any registered person with customer contact, plus their immediate supervisors — and mark each row in or out with the reason.
Cross-check against the payroll roster from the HRIS so contractors and dual-hatted insurance producers are not missed.
Hand the signed covered-population file to the Learning Development Manager with the extract date on it.
checklist.done: a dated covered-population file derived from CRD and reconciled to payroll is signed and handed over.

checklist.step: Turn the needs analysis into module specifications
actions: Take each need from the approved needs analysis and write a module specification with learning objectives, duration and the assessment questions that prove the objective was met.

Build the variable annuity module around the features that generate complaints: surrender charge schedules, living benefit rider mechanics, exchange and replacement analysis under Rule 2330, and fee disclosure.
Build the communications module around Rule 2210(d)(1) content standards and the Rule 2211 treatment of guarantees and hypothetical illustrations.
Send the specifications to Compliance for content sign-off before build starts.
checklist.done: each identified need has a module specification with objectives, duration and assessment items signed off by Compliance.

checklist.step: Get the module content reviewed for regulatory accuracy
actions: Read every slide, script and assessment item against the current rule text and correct any statement that overstates a guarantee or understates a charge.
Confirm the module names the actual products the firm distributes rather than generic examples, so representatives train on what they sell.
Record the review on a content sign-off sheet with the reviewer name, date and the module version reviewed.
Return anything citing a superseded rule number for rework before publication.
checklist.done: every module version carries a dated compliance content sign-off referencing the current rule text.

checklist.step: Publish and configure the modules in the learning management system
actions: Load each module into the learning management system with the version number in the title and the Firm Element year as a category tag.
Set the assessment pass mark and the retake rules, and enable attempt logging so partial completions are visible.
Configure the due date as 31 December of the plan year and enable the reminder cadence at 60, 30 and 10 days out.
Run a test enrolment yourself and confirm the completion record writes with a timestamp and a score.
checklist.done: modules are published with version, due date, pass mark and reminders configured, proven by a test enrolment.

checklist.step: Assign the plan to the covered population
actions: Load the covered-population file as the assignment audience and confirm the learning management system headcount matches the file headcount exactly before releasing.
Apply the differentiated assignments the plan sets — variable annuity sellers get the product module, supervising principals additionally get the supervision module.
Release the assignments and export the assignment confirmation list as the baseline coverage evidence.
Send each supervising principal their team's assignment list.
checklist.done: assignments are released, headcount matches the covered-population file, and each supervisor holds their team list.

checklist.step: Catch mid-year joiners within 30 days of registration
actions: Run a weekly CRD registration-approval report in FINRA Gateway and send new approvals to Learning and Development the same week.
Confirm each new covered registered person receives the Firm Element assignment within 30 days of registration approval.
Where a joiner registers in December, shorten the due date to the earlier of 31 December or 30 days from approval and tell their supervisor immediately.
Log the registration date and the assignment date side by side so the 30-day gap is evidenced.
checklist.done: every mid-year registrant is assigned within 30 days of approval with both dates logged.

checklist.step: Reconcile leavers and Form U5 terminations out of the population
actions: Take the Form U5 filings made in the year from FINRA Gateway and match each to the covered-population file.
Close out the assignment for anyone terminated before their due date and record the termination date as the reason — do not simply delete the row.
Keep the completion record for leavers who did complete, since the CE record follows the individual.
Reconcile the year-end population as opening headcount plus joiners minus leavers and prove it ties to CRD.
checklist.done: the year-end covered population ties to CRD as opening plus joiners minus leavers, with every closure reasoned.

checklist.step: Chase incomplete learners on the reminder cadence
actions: Run the incomplete-assignment report weekly from October and send each learner a direct reminder naming the module and the 31 December deadline.
Copy the supervising principal at the 30-day and 10-day marks — supervision of completion is the principal's obligation, not a courtesy.
Escalate anyone still incomplete at 10 December to the Head of Compliance with a named reason per person.
Keep every reminder and escalation in the evidence file.
checklist.done: the reminder and escalation cadence is evidenced per learner, with a named reason for anyone incomplete at 10 December.

checklist.step: Restrict activity for anyone incomplete at the deadline
actions: On 2 January take the final incomplete list and impose a written restriction on securities activity for each person until the module is completed.
Notify the individual, the supervising principal and the Distribution Operations Manager the same day, and confirm order-entry entitlements are suspended.
Record the restriction start date, the completion date and the lift date for each person.
Require a written explanation from each supervising principal whose team member missed the deadline.
checklist.done: every 31 December incompletion carries a dated written restriction, suspended entitlements and a supervisor explanation.

checklist.step: Track the separate Regulatory Element obligation alongside Firm Element
actions: Pull the FINRA Gateway CE Status report showing each registered person's annual Regulatory Element requirement and its 31 December due date.
Chase anyone not yet complete on the FINRA Financial Professional Gateway, since failure moves the registration to CE Inactive.
Record Regulatory Element status against the same roster used for Firm Element so a single view shows both.
Escalate anyone approaching CE Inactive to the Head of Compliance before year end.
checklist.done: every registered person's Regulatory Element status is tracked to 31 December alongside their Firm Element status.

checklist.step: Assemble the Firm Element evidence file
actions: Assemble the year's file: needs analysis memo, approved training plan, module outlines with version numbers, content sign-offs, covered-population file, assignment extract, completion extract with timestamps and scores, reminders, escalations and restrictions.
Export the completion extract directly from the learning management system to a locked format and record the export timestamp — later hand edits destroy its evidential value.
Reconcile the completion count to the year-end covered population and state the completion percentage on the file cover sheet.
Route the file to the Head of Compliance for acceptance.
checklist.done: a single evidence file reconciles population to completions, carries a locked system extract and is accepted by Compliance.

checklist.step: Report Firm Element results into supervisory governance
actions: Include completion rates by branch and by supervising principal in the Rule 3120 annual report of the supervisory control system.
Name branches with repeated incompletions as a supervisory control weakness rather than a training statistic.
Give the Head of Compliance the figures for the Rule 3130 certification discussion with the Chief Executive Officer.
Record the committee acceptance date.
checklist.done: completion rates by branch and principal appear in the Rule 3120 report and are minuted.

checklist.step: Feed the year's failures back into next year's needs analysis
actions: Extract assessment item-level results and identify the questions the population failed most often.
Add each weak area, plus the year's complaints and internal inspection findings, to the input pack for next year's needs analysis.
Where a module scored high but complaints continued in that area, mark the module as ineffective and require a redesign rather than a re-run.
Hand the input pack to Compliance by 1 September so the next cycle can close by 31 December.
checklist.done: an input pack of weak assessment areas and complaint themes is delivered by 1 September for the next cycle.

checklist.step: Version and archive the module content
actions: Archive each delivered module version, its content sign-off and its assessment bank, since a later examination asks what was actually taught that year, not what is taught now.
Apply the six-year retention label and index by plan year, module name and version.
Confirm superseded versions remain retrievable and are not overwritten by the current release.
Record the archive reference on the evidence file cover sheet.
checklist.done: each delivered module version is archived under six-year retention and retrievable by plan year and version.

checklist.step: Close the year and open the next plan cycle
actions: Mark the plan year closed in the learning management system so no completion can be back-dated into it.
Publish the final completion percentage and the outstanding restriction list to the Head of Compliance and the supervising principals.
Open the next plan year record and load the 1 September needs-analysis milestone and the 31 December delivery deadline.
Carry every unlifted restriction into the new year as an open item.
checklist.done: the plan year is locked, final results published, and the next cycle's milestones are in the calendar.

testing.step: Rebuild the covered population from CRD independently
actions: Export the firm's registered person roster for the year directly from FINRA Gateway CRD, including joiners and leavers, with registration categories.
Apply the Rule 1240(b) covered-person definition yourself and build your own population before looking at the firm's file.
Reconcile your count to the firm's covered-population file and investigate every difference by name.
testing.done: an independently built covered population reconciles to the firm's file with every difference explained by name.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to payroll and to Form U4/U5 activity
actions: Pull the HRIS roster for the year and match to the CRD population; investigate anyone with customer contact in HRIS but absent from the registered roster.
Match Form U4 approvals to the joiner list and Form U5 filings to the leaver list.
Confirm the year-end population equals opening plus joiners minus leavers and that the arithmetic is shown, not asserted.
testing.done: the population arithmetic ties to HRIS, U4 approvals and U5 filings with the working shown.

testing.step: Test assignment coverage across the whole population
actions: Export the assignment list from the learning management system and match every covered person to at least one Firm Element assignment.
List anyone never assigned — coverage failures are absolute and need no sampling.
Confirm differentiated assignments landed correctly: variable annuity sellers hold the product module and supervising principals hold the supervision module.
testing.done: every covered person holds the correct assignments, or the omission is listed as an automatic fail.

testing.step: Draw the completion sample and document the method
actions: Take 100% of persons recorded incomplete at 31 December and 100% of December joiners.
Take 25 completions by seeded random selection across branches, weighted toward branches with the highest complaint counts.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all incompletions and December joiners is documented with its seed.

testing.step: Re-perform the completion evidence on the sample
actions: For each sampled person open the learning management system transcript and read the module version, attempt history, score and completion timestamp.
Confirm the completion timestamp is on or before 31 December and that the module completed is the one the plan assigned, not a substitute.
Challenge completions with an implausible elapsed time against the module duration, since click-through completion defeats the rule's purpose.
Screenshot each transcript into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled completion is verified on module version, score, elapsed time and a pre-31-December timestamp.

testing.step: Recompute the mid-year 30-day assignment maths
actions: For each joiner, recompute assignment due date as CRD registration approval date plus 30 days and compare to the actual assignment date.
List every assignment made after day 30 with its day count.
For December registrants confirm the due date was shortened to the earlier of 31 December or approval plus 30 days.
testing.done: every joiner's 30-day assignment clock is recomputed and each overrun is listed with its day count.

testing.step: Verify the needs analysis genuinely drove the plan
actions: Read the needs analysis and confirm every need it identified appears as a module in the approved plan.
Confirm the analysis is dated before the plan approval date — a plan approved first and rationalised later fails Rule 1240(b).
Trace three named needs back to their source evidence: a specific complaint, an inspection finding or a product launch.
Flag any module in the plan that answers no identified need as unexplained content.
testing.done: each need maps to a module, the analysis pre-dates the plan, and three needs trace to named source evidence.

testing.step: Test the restrictions imposed on year-end incompletions
actions: For each 31 December incompletion, obtain the written restriction, its start date and the entitlement suspension confirmation.
Check the order-entry and new-business systems to confirm the person transacted nothing between the restriction date and the completion date.
Any securities activity during the restriction period is a reportable supervisory breach, not a test exception.
Confirm the supervising principal's written explanation exists for each case.
testing.done: every incompletion carries a dated restriction with no activity during the restricted period.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the person, the failure type and whether it is a coverage, timing or evidence failure.
Assign a root cause — population derived from the wrong roster, joiner feed missed, supervisor never chased, module version mismatch — and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and require completion inside 30 days for anyone still untrained.
Carry open exceptions into the next annual test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute assignment coverage and 31 December completion percentages against the 100% threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references behind each figure.
Have the Internal Auditor, who sits outside Learning and Development and Compliance plan approval, sign the workpaper.
Report the result into the Rule 3120 supervisory control report and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states coverage and completion percentages, a conclusion and the Rule 3120 reporting reference.

checklist.step: Screen the candidate before any Form U4 is filed
actions: Collect the candidate's ten-year employment and residential history, and the disclosure questionnaire covering criminal, regulatory, civil judicial, customer complaint, bankruptcy, bond and judgment/lien events.
Order the fingerprint submission through FINRA's electronic fingerprint process and record the submission date — the person cannot be associated without it.
Request the prior firm's Form U5 from CRD and compare its disclosures against the candidate's answers, resolving every difference in writing before filing.
Escalate any answer suggesting a statutory disqualification to Regulatory Counsel before proceeding.
checklist.done: employment history, disclosure answers, fingerprints and the prior U5 are reconciled with all differences resolved in writing.

checklist.step: File the Form U4 and request the correct registration categories
actions: In FINRA Gateway open CRD, create the Form U4 and complete the identifying, employment, other business activity and disclosure sections from the screening pack.
Request the registration categories the role actually needs — Series 6 or 7 for variable contract sales, Series 26 or 24 for principals — plus the jurisdictions the person will do business in.
Attach the disclosure reporting pages for every 'yes' answer with the full narrative rather than a summary, since incomplete disclosure is itself a violation.
Submit, pay the filing and registration fees from the firm's flex-funding account, and record the CRD number and filing date.
checklist.done: the Form U4 is filed with the correct categories and jurisdictions, complete disclosure pages, and the CRD number recorded.

checklist.step: Confirm qualification examinations and any waiver before permitting activity
actions: Check the CRD exam window opened by the U4 filing and confirm the Securities Industry Essentials examination plus the required representative or principal examination are passed and recorded.

Where the candidate relies on the two-year qualification window after a prior termination, or on the Maintaining Qualifications Program, verify the eligibility date in CRD rather than accepting the candidate's word.
Where a waiver is sought, file the waiver request through FINRA Gateway with the supporting experience evidence and track it to decision.
Do not release order-entry or new-business entitlements until CRD shows the registration approved.
checklist.done: CRD shows every required examination passed or a granted waiver, and entitlements are released only after approval.

checklist.step: Pair the securities registration with the state insurance licence and appointment
actions: In the NIPR Gateway confirm the individual holds a resident life licence with the variable contracts line of authority in their home state, plus non-resident licences for every state they will solicit in.
Submit the carrier appointment through NIPR Producer Appointment for each writing company and state, inside the state's appointment deadline after the first application is submitted.
Load the licence numbers, lines of authority and appointment effective dates into the producer management system and link them to the CRD number.
Block commission payment until both the securities registration and the state appointment are active.
checklist.done: the person holds an active variable contracts licence and a state appointment for every writing company, linked to their CRD record.

checklist.step: File Form BR for every branch and office of supervisory jurisdiction
actions: Apply the Rule 3110(f) definitions to each location and decide whether it is an OSJ, a supervisory branch, a non-supervisory branch or an excluded location.
File Form BR in CRD within 30 days of opening, relocating or closing a location, naming the branch manager and their CRD number.
Register the location with each state that requires separate branch registration and pay the state branch fees.
Update the branch list in the producer management system and confirm every registered person is mapped to a registered location.
checklist.done: every operating location has a Form BR filed within 30 days and every registered person maps to a registered location.

checklist.step: Amend Form U4 within 30 days of any reportable event
actions: Run the monthly attestation asking every registered person to confirm or update outside business activities, private securities transactions, residential address, and any new criminal, civil, regulatory, complaint, bankruptcy, lien or judgment event.
On learning of a reportable event, file the U4 amendment in CRD within 30 days, and within 10 business days where the event creates a statutory disqualification.
Record the date the firm learned of the event separately from the filing date so the day count is provable.
Route every disclosure event to Regulatory Counsel before filing where the answer could trigger a Form MC-400 eligibility proceeding.
checklist.done: every reportable event is amended in CRD inside its window, with the learn date and filing date both recorded.

checklist.step: File Form U5 within 30 days of any termination
actions: Take the weekly termination feed from HR and file the Form U5 in CRD within 30 days of the termination date.
Complete the reason for termination accurately — voluntary, permitted to resign, discharged, or terminated after allegations — and attach disclosure pages where an internal review is open.
Where an internal review concludes after filing, file the amended U5 within 30 days of that conclusion.
Deliver a copy of the U5 to the former representative within 30 days as the rule requires and retain proof of delivery.
checklist.done: every termination has a U5 filed and delivered inside 30 days with an accurate stated reason.

checklist.step: Work the annual registration renewal cycle to protect membership standing
actions: Download the FINRA Preliminary Renewal Statement in FINRA Gateway when it publishes in November and reconcile the listed registrations, branches and jurisdictions to the internal roster.
Terminate registrations for people and jurisdictions no longer needed before the renewal cut-off so the firm does not pay for and carry dead registrations.
Fund the flex-funding account and pay the renewal statement by the FINRA December deadline — non-payment leaves registrations ineligible on 1 January.
Reconcile the Final Renewal Statement in January and clear any difference within the month.
checklist.done: the preliminary statement is reconciled, paid by the December deadline, and the final statement is cleared in January.

checklist.step: Maintain CE status so no registration goes CE Inactive
actions: Run the FINRA Gateway CE Status report monthly and list anyone whose annual Regulatory Element is outstanding.
Chase them to complete on the FINRA Financial Professional Gateway well before 31 December, since a missed year makes the registration CE Inactive on 1 January.
Where a person goes CE Inactive, suspend order-entry entitlements the same day and notify their supervising principal in writing.
Record the inactive date, completion date and reactivation date for each case.
checklist.done: CE status is monitored monthly and any CE Inactive registration is suspended the same day with dates recorded.

checklist.step: Apply the Rule 1017 materiality test to business and ownership changes
actions: Screen every proposed change against the Rule 1017(a) triggers: merger, acquisition of assets, direct or indirect change in equity ownership or partnership capital of 25% or more, and material change in business operations.

Test business-operation changes against the Rule 1011(k) definition — removing a membership agreement restriction, adding market making or underwriting, or adding a new product line such as a new variable product distribution arrangement.
Write a materiality memo naming the trigger relied on or the reason none applies, and have Regulatory Counsel clear it.
Where material, do not implement until FINRA approves — a safe-harbour expansion is the only exception and its limits must be cited.
checklist.done: every proposed change carries a counsel-cleared materiality memo and no material change proceeds before approval.

checklist.step: File and run the Rule 1017 continuing membership application
actions: File the continuing membership application through the FINRA Gateway Membership Application Program with the business plan, pro forma financials, supervisory procedures and organisational chart.
Track FINRA's request-for-information cycle and answer each request inside the stated deadline, logging the request date and response date.
Record any restriction FINRA imposes in the amended membership agreement and push it into the WSPs and system controls the same month.
Confirm the effective date of approval before the business change goes live.
checklist.done: the application is filed, every information request answered on time, and the amended membership agreement is reflected in the WSPs.

checklist.step: Keep the membership contact and emergency information current
actions: Review the FINRA Contact System entries in FINRA Gateway at least annually and after any change of officer: executive representative, chief compliance officer, and the two Rule 4370 emergency contacts.
Confirm the executive representative designation matches the officer the board appointed, and update the record within the required window after any change.
Verify the firm's main address, mailing address and website of record are correct, since FINRA notices go to the address on file.
Record the review date and reviewer.
checklist.done: all FINRA contact records are verified current with a dated annual review and post-change updates.

checklist.step: Reconcile who is actually transacting against who is registered
actions: Monthly, extract the producers who submitted variable annuity or variable life business and match each to an active CRD registration and an active state appointment for the writing company and state.
Suspend any producer transacting without both, hold the business, and refer the case to Compliance the same day.
Reconcile the commission payment file to the same match so unlicensed commission is never paid.
Record the monthly match rate and the names of every break.
checklist.done: every producer with submitted business is matched monthly to an active registration and appointment, with breaks suspended same day.

checklist.step: Escalate statutory disqualification and unregistered activity
actions: On any event that may cause statutory disqualification, take Regulatory Counsel's assessment and decide whether to file Form MC-400 or to terminate the association.
Report unregistered activity as a Rule 4530(b) self-identified violation where the conclusion is reached, and start that 30-day clock.
Remediate the affected customer transactions rather than leaving them on the books unsupervised.
Record the decision, its date and the customers affected.
checklist.done: every disqualification event and instance of unregistered activity has a dated decision, a filing route and customer remediation.

checklist.step: Archive the registration evidence for the retention period
actions: Archive per person the U4 and amendments, fingerprint results, examination records, U5 and delivery proof, plus per branch the Form BR filings, under FINRA/registration/<CRD number>.
Apply the association-plus-three-years retention label required by SEA Rule 17a-4(e)(1) and hold the membership agreement and Rule 1017 approvals for the life of the enterprise.
Confirm records are retrievable by name, CRD number and branch code.
Record the archive reference on the producer management system record.
checklist.done: registration records are archived under the correct retention labels and retrievable by CRD number and branch code.

testing.step: Build the registration and filing population from CRD
actions: Export from FINRA Gateway CRD the firm's registered person roster, all U4 amendments, all U5 filings and all Form BR filings for the period, with filing dates.
Export the branch list and the jurisdictions each registration covers.
Record the extract date and counts so the population is reproducible.
testing.done: a dated CRD-sourced population of registrations, filings and branches exists with recorded counts.

testing.step: Reconcile the CRD roster to HR, payroll and the producer system
actions: Match the CRD roster to the HRIS active-employee list and the producer management system to find anyone associated but not registered.
Match terminations in HRIS to U5 filings and list any termination with no U5.
Match the firm's operating locations from facilities and the branch list to Form BR filings and list any unregistered location.
Agree every break in writing with the Producer Compliance Manager before sampling.
testing.done: the roster, terminations and locations reconcile to CRD with every break documented and agreed.

testing.step: Draw the filing sample and document the method
actions: Take 100% of U4 amendments carrying a disclosure event and 100% of U5 filings with a discharge or allegation reason.
Take 25 further filings by seeded random selection across U4, U5 and BR.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all disclosure amendments and adverse U5s is documented with its seed.

testing.step: Recompute the 30-day and 10-business-day filing clocks
actions: For each sampled U4 amendment, recompute due date as the date the firm learned of the event plus 30 days, and compare it to the CRD filing date.
For statutory disqualification events recompute against the 10-business-day window using the firm's business-day calendar.
For U5s recompute from the termination date and for Form BR from the open, relocate or close date, each plus 30 days.
Challenge any 'learn date' later than the underlying document date — a shifted learn date is the usual way a late filing looks timely.
testing.done: every sampled filing clock is recomputed from source dates and each overrun is listed with its day count.

testing.step: Re-perform the disclosure completeness check in CRD
actions: For each sampled disclosure event, read the source document — court order, regulatory letter, complaint, judgment — and compare it to the disclosure reporting page filed in CRD.
Confirm the narrative states the facts, the disposition and the amounts, rather than summarising the event away.
Compare the filed answers to the prior firm's U5 disclosures where the person joined during the period.
Screenshot the CRD disclosure page into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled disclosure is traced to its source document with content compared field by field.

testing.step: Test registration and appointment status against actual transactions
actions: Extract every variable annuity and variable life application submitted in the period with the submitting producer, the writing company, the state and the submission date.
For each, confirm the producer's CRD registration was approved and the NIPR state appointment was effective on the submission date, not merely today.
Any transaction before registration approval or appointment effective date is a reportable breach requiring customer remediation, not a test exception.
Reconcile the commission payment file to the same test to find unlicensed commission.
testing.done: every sampled transaction is matched to an active registration and appointment as at the submission date.

testing.step: Verify branch registration and supervisory coverage
actions: For each operating location, confirm a Form BR exists, the designation as OSJ or branch matches the supervisory activity actually performed there, and a named branch manager with an appropriate principal registration is recorded.
Confirm every registered person is mapped to a registered location and none is mapped to a closed one.
Test three locations against the Rule 3110(f) definitions to confirm the designation is not understated to avoid inspection obligations.
testing.done: every location has a matching Form BR, a qualified named manager, and a designation that matches its actual activity.

testing.step: Test the Rule 1017 materiality judgements and the renewal cycle
actions: List every ownership, control or business change considered during the period and read the materiality memo for each against Rule 1017(a) and the Rule 1011(k) definition.
Confirm no material change went live before FINRA's approval date, and where a safe harbour was relied on confirm the numeric limits were actually met.
Confirm the membership agreement on file reflects every approval and restriction, and that the restrictions appear in the WSPs.
Confirm the Preliminary Renewal Statement was reconciled and paid by the December deadline and the Final Renewal Statement cleared in January.
testing.done: every change carries a supported materiality conclusion, no material change pre-dates approval, and the renewal cycle is evidenced.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the person or location, the filing missed, the day count and any customer transactions affected.
Assign a root cause — attestation not run, HR feed missed, learn date not captured, appointment ordered late, materiality asserted without counsel — and a named owner.
Set a remediation date, and for unregistered activity open the Rule 4530(b) assessment immediately rather than waiting.
Carry open exceptions into the next quarter's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the on-time filing rate, the unregistered-activity count and the branch coverage rate against the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper sections behind each figure.
Have the Internal Auditor, who filed none of the sampled forms, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report to the Compliance Committee and include registration findings in the Rule 3120 supervisory control report.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the filing rate, unregistered-activity count, a conclusion and the committee reporting date.
