checklist.step: Intake the communication and classify it under Rule 2210(a)
actions: Open the review request in the marketing automation platform and capture the asset, the intended audience, the channel and the planned first-use date.
Classify the asset as retail communication, correspondence or institutional communication, applying the 25-retail-investor-in-30-calendar-days test to anything sent individually.
Record the product it concerns — variable annuity, variable life, or a non-registered product — because Rule 2211 and the Rule 2210(c)(3) filing route turn on that.
Reject undated, unsourced drafts back to the Marketing Manager rather than starting the clock on incomplete material.
checklist.done: the asset is logged with a classification, audience, channel, product type and planned first-use date.

checklist.step: Assemble the substantiation file behind every claim
actions: List every factual claim, statistic, ranking, performance figure and guarantee reference in the asset on a substantiation sheet.

Get the source for each from the owning team — separate account performance from the Investment Operations Manager, rider mechanics and charges from the Insurance Product Manager, ratings from the source agency's own publication.
Record the as-of date for every figure and the date the figure expires, since stale performance is the most common Advertising Regulation comment.
Refuse to progress the review while any claim remains unsourced.
checklist.done: every claim on the substantiation sheet has a named source, an as-of date and an expiry date.

checklist.step: Apply the Rule 2210(d)(1) content standards checklist
actions: Work the checklist line by line: fair and balanced, provides a sound basis for evaluating the facts, no false, exaggerated, unwarranted, promissory or misleading statement, no prediction or projection of performance, no omission of material information that makes it misleading.
Confirm the firm's name is prominent, any relationship with another entity is disclosed, and the audience can tell who is speaking.
Confirm risks are presented with comparable prominence to benefits rather than in a footnote.
Annotate each checklist line with the location in the asset that satisfies it.
checklist.done: every content-standard line is answered with a pinpoint reference into the asset.

checklist.step: Apply the Rule 2211 variable product requirements
actions: Confirm the communication does not represent the variable contract as a mutual fund, a savings account, or a short-term liquid investment.
Confirm every guarantee is attributed to the claims-paying ability of the issuing insurance company and that the guarantee's conditions and limits are stated with it.
Check hypothetical illustrations use permitted assumed rates, reflect all charges including mortality and expense, contract, and rider fees, and carry the required explanatory disclosure.
Confirm surrender charge periods, withdrawal restrictions and the tax treatment of withdrawals appear where the material discusses access to money.
checklist.done: guarantees, illustrations, charges and liquidity limitations are presented as Rule 2211 requires, with each point evidenced in the asset.

checklist.step: Check the prospectus and disclosure linkage
actions: Confirm the material is preceded or accompanied by the current statutory or summary prospectus for the contract and the underlying portfolios, or contains the required directions to obtain it.
Verify the prospectus edition date cited is the one currently effective on EDGAR for the registration statement.
Confirm the contract and share class named in the material is the one actually offered in the states the campaign targets.
Record the prospectus edition date on the review record.
checklist.done: the current prospectus is linked or delivered and its edition date matches the effective filing on EDGAR.

checklist.step: Obtain the registered principal's written pre-approval
actions: Read the asset, the substantiation sheet and the completed checklists as the approving principal — approval is a judgement, not a countersignature.
Apply the Rule 2210(b)(1) timing: approve in writing before the earlier of first use or filing with FINRA, and never retrospectively.
Record the approval with your name, CRD number, registration category, date and the exact asset version approved.
Reject and return anything where a checklist line is unanswered or a claim is unsourced.
checklist.done: the exact asset version carries a dated written approval naming the principal and their CRD number, before first use.

checklist.step: File the communication with FINRA Advertising Regulation
actions: In FINRA Gateway open the Advertising Regulation electronic filing application and start a new filing for the approved asset.

Select the correct filing type — post-use within 10 business days of first use for retail communications concerning variable insurance products under Rule 2210(c)(3), or pre-use at least 10 business days before first use where the new-member requirement or a spot-check letter applies.
Attach the asset exactly as used, the statement of first use date, the supporting prospectus reference and the filing fee.
Record the FINRA filing reference number and submission date on the communication register.
checklist.done: the filing is submitted in the correct route with the asset as used, and its reference number is on the register.

checklist.step: Compute and monitor the 10-business-day filing clock
actions: On approval, set the filing due date at first-use date plus 10 business days using the firm's business-day calendar including exchange holidays.
Monitor the queue daily and escalate anything unfiled at business day 9 to the Head of Compliance.
Where first use slipped, restate the due date from the actual first-use date evidenced by the campaign send log, not the planned date.
Record first-use date, filing date and the day count on the register for every filed item.
checklist.done: every filable item shows a first-use date, a filing date and a day count of 10 business days or fewer.

checklist.step: Work FINRA comment letters to closure
actions: On receipt of an Advertising Regulation comment letter, log the letter date and the response deadline it states.
Withdraw or suspend the asset from circulation the same day where the staff object to a claim, and confirm the marketing automation platform has stopped further sends.
Revise the asset, obtain fresh principal approval on the revised version, and file the revision citing the original filing reference.
Record the closing letter and file the whole exchange with the communication.
checklist.done: each comment letter has a suspension, a revised and re-approved asset, a refiling and a recorded closure.

checklist.step: Control what the field actually uses
actions: Publish only approved, in-date assets to the broker and agent portal, each tagged with its approval date, filing reference and expiry date.
Disable download of any asset past its expiry or withdrawn after a comment letter, and notify the wholesalers who downloaded it.
Prohibit field-created material by policy and route any request for a custom piece back through the review gate.
Report portal download statistics to Compliance monthly so use can be reconciled to approvals.
checklist.done: the field portal carries only approved, in-date assets, with withdrawn material disabled and downloaders notified.

checklist.step: Review correspondence and social media under Rule 3110(b)(4)
actions: Run the lexicon-based surveillance over representative email and the archived social media channels for terms such as guaranteed, risk-free, no fees, and beat the market.
Review the flagged items, plus a random sample of unflagged correspondence, and document the reviewer, date and disposition of each.
Escalate any static social media content that meets the retail communication definition into the principal approval and filing route.
Report review volumes and findings monthly to the supervising principal.
checklist.done: correspondence and social media are reviewed on a documented lexicon plus random basis with dispositions recorded.

checklist.step: Expire and refresh dated content on schedule
actions: Run the expiry report monthly for assets whose performance data, rates or ratings pass their stated as-of window.
Pull expiring assets from all channels — portal, website, email templates, printed inventory — before the expiry date rather than after.
Route refreshed versions back through substantiation, checklist, principal approval and filing as new material.
Record the withdrawal date for each expired asset.
checklist.done: no asset remains in any channel past its data expiry date, and refreshes re-enter the full approval route.

checklist.step: Report communications metrics into supervisory governance
actions: Report monthly to the supervising principal: assets reviewed, rejected, approved, filed, filed late, comment letters received and open.
Include repeat content failures by originating team so the training need is visible rather than absorbed by the reviewers.
Feed the year's figures into the Rule 3120 annual report of the supervisory control system.
Record the committee acceptance date.
checklist.done: monthly metrics reach the supervising principal and the year's figures appear in the Rule 3120 report.

checklist.step: Retain the communication record for three years from last use
actions: Archive per asset: the version as used, the substantiation sheet, the completed checklists, the dated principal approval, the FINRA filing reference and any comment letter exchange.
Apply the Rule 2210(b)(4) retention of three years from date of last use, the first two years in an easily accessible place.
Record the date of last use as the withdrawal date so the retention clock is calculable.
Confirm assets are retrievable by product, channel, approval date and filing reference.
checklist.done: each asset's full review record is archived with a recorded last-use date and a three-year retention label.

checklist.step: Refresh the reviewer checklist when the rules or the staff view move
actions: Review FINRA Advertising Regulation Regulatory Notices, interpretive letters and the annual report of common findings at least annually.
Amend the reviewer checklist to add each new failure mode as its own line, and version the checklist with an effective date.
Brief every reviewer and approving principal on what changed and from which date it applies.
Retire superseded checklist versions to the archive so past reviews can still be judged on the standard then in force.
checklist.done: the checklist is versioned annually against current FINRA guidance and every reviewer is briefed on the changes.

testing.step: Build the population of communications first used in the quarter
actions: Extract every campaign send, landing page publication and asset release from the marketing automation platform with its first-use date and audience size.
Add website change logs, paid media schedules, seminar bookings and broker portal publications for the same period.
Add the archived social media posts for the firm and its registered representatives so field-originated content is in scope.
testing.done: a multi-channel first-use population is assembled with dates and audience sizes and its counts recorded.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the communications register
actions: Match every population item to a communications register entry on asset name and version.
List any item used with no register entry — unreviewed material in circulation is the failure this test exists to find.
Check the reverse: register entries approved but never used, which distort the filing population.
Agree the reconciliation with the Marketing Compliance Analyst before sampling.
testing.done: every used communication is matched to a register entry or listed as a completeness exception.

testing.step: Draw the sample and document the method
actions: Take 100% of variable annuity and variable life retail communications containing performance figures, living benefit descriptions or the word guarantee.
Take 20 further items by seeded random selection across email, portal, website and social channels.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all performance and guarantee material is documented with its seed.

testing.step: Verify principal pre-approval on the exact version used
actions: For each sampled item, open the approval record and compare the approved version hash or file to the version actually sent or published.
Confirm the approval date is earlier than the first-use date and earlier than the filing date.
Confirm the approver held a Series 24 or Series 26 principal registration active on the approval date by checking CRD.
Treat a post-use approval as a fail, not a timing observation.
testing.done: each sampled item has a pre-use approval on the exact version used by a principal registered on that date.

testing.step: Re-perform the content review independently
actions: Read each sampled asset against Rule 2210(d)(1) and Rule 2211 without opening the reviewer's checklist first, and record your own conclusions.
Test each performance figure, ranking and guarantee statement back to the substantiation sheet source and its as-of date.
Confirm risk and benefit are presented with comparable prominence and that no statement implies a projection of performance.
Record every difference from the reviewer's conclusion as an exception, including 'right conclusion, no support on file'.
testing.done: each sampled asset has an independent content conclusion recorded against the reviewer's, with claims traced to source.

testing.step: Recompute the filing clocks and trace to FINRA references
actions: For each filable item recompute the due date as first-use date plus 10 business days using the exchange holiday calendar.
Compare to the recorded filing date and list every item filed on business day 11 or later with its day count.
Verify each recorded filing reference exists by opening the submission in FINRA Gateway Advertising Regulation and matching product, asset title and submission date.
Test the pre-file route separately where the new-member or spot-check requirement applied, confirming the 10-business-day lead was actually taken.
testing.done: every filing clock is recomputed, every filing reference verified in FINRA Gateway, and late filings listed with day counts.

testing.step: Test comment letter handling and asset withdrawal
actions: List every Advertising Regulation comment letter received in the period with its date and stated response deadline.
Confirm the asset was suspended on the letter date by checking the marketing automation platform send history and the portal availability log.
Confirm the revised version obtained fresh principal approval and was refiled citing the original reference, and that the file holds a closing letter.
List any asset that continued to circulate after a comment letter as a reportable breach.
testing.done: each comment letter shows same-day suspension, a re-approved revision, a refiling and a recorded closure.

testing.step: Test correspondence and field-originated material
actions: Take the Rule 3110(b)(4) review logs and confirm the lexicon list, the sampling rate and the reviewer dispositions are documented.
Select 20 flagged items and confirm each has a reviewer, a date and a disposition, and that escalated items reached the principal approval route.
Apply the 25-retail-investor-in-30-days test to the correspondence population to find items that should have been treated as retail communications.
Check representative social media archives for static content promoting variable products with no approval record.
testing.done: correspondence and field material are tested for reviewer coverage and for misclassified retail communications.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the asset, the channel, the failure type and the audience reached.
Assign a root cause — used before approval, wrong classification, unsourced claim, expired data, filing queue not worked — and a named owner.
Set a remediation date, and for material misstatement decide the recall and, where customers relied on it, the customer remediation.
Carry open exceptions into the next quarter's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the pre-approval rate, the within-10-business-day filing rate and the content exception rate against the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper sections behind each figure.
Have the Compliance Officer, who approved none of the sampled communications, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report to the Compliance Committee and fold the figures into the Rule 3120 supervisory control report.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the approval, filing and content rates, a conclusion and the committee reporting date.
