checklist.step: Maintain the written supervisory procedures that carry each obligation
actions: Keep the WSP section for each supervised activity naming the supervisory step, the title of the principal who performs it, the frequency, and the record that evidences it, as Rule 3110(b)(1) requires.
Amend the section within 30 days of any rule change or new product launch and version the document with an effective date.
Record the designated principal by name and CRD number for every branch and every activity, and reassign within five business days of any departure.
Publish the current version to the intranet and archive the superseded one.
checklist.done: every supervised activity has a current WSP section naming the step, the principal, the frequency and the evidence record.

checklist.step: Run principal review of every deferred variable annuity application inside seven business days
actions: Take applications from the new business queue with the date the office of supervisory jurisdiction received a complete and correct application stamped on each — that stamp starts the Rule 2330(c) seven-business-day clock.
Review the customer's age, annuitisation intent, liquidity needs, and whether the contract's fees, surrender period and riders are consistent with the recorded investment profile.
Record the reviewing principal's name, CRD number, decision and date on the transaction record before the application is transmitted to the issuer.
Reject and return incomplete applications rather than pausing the clock informally.
checklist.done: every deferred variable annuity application shows a principal decision recorded within seven business days of the OSJ receipt date.

checklist.step: Test exchanges and replacements before they are transmitted
actions: For every exchange, capture the surrender charge on the existing contract, the new surrender period, the loss of any living or death benefit, and the difference in total annual charges.
Confirm the Rule 2330(b)(1)(A)(iii) test — whether the customer has had another exchange within the preceding 36 months — using the producer's disclosure and the customer's own records.
Confirm the replacement disclosure required by the state insurance replacement regulation was signed and dated by the customer before the application.
Decline any exchange where the surrender cost is not offset by a stated, documented benefit.
checklist.done: every exchange carries a documented cost comparison, a 36-month exchange history and a signed replacement disclosure.

checklist.step: Operate the exception surveillance reports daily
actions: Run the standing exception set daily: exchanges within 36 months, contracts sold to customers over 75, concentration above the firm's percentage-of-liquid-net-worth threshold, riders elected for customers outside the rider's benefit window, and unusually high production concentrated in one producer.
Record the threshold behind each report and the date it was last calibrated, since a threshold nobody can explain is not a control.
Assign each alert to the supervising principal with a 10-business-day disposition deadline.
Escalate alerts unworked at day 8 to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: the exception set runs daily on documented thresholds and every alert is assigned with a 10-business-day deadline.

checklist.step: Disposition each alert with reasoning, not a status flag
actions: For each alert open a case and record the facts examined: the customer profile, the transaction terms, the producer's explanation and the customer's own confirmation where obtained.
State the conclusion — no concern, coaching, restriction, or escalation to investigation — with the reason, and name the principal who decided.
Where the customer is contacted, record who spoke to them, on what date, and what they said, in their words.
Close only when the reasoning would satisfy an examiner reading it cold two years later.
checklist.done: every alert closes with recorded facts, a named decider and a stated reason rather than a status change.

checklist.step: Inspect offices of supervisory jurisdiction and branches on the Rule 3110(c) cycle
actions: Maintain the inspection calendar: each OSJ and each supervisory branch at least annually, each non-supervisory branch at least every three years, with the due date derived from the last inspection date.

Inspect on the required scope — safeguarding of customer funds and securities, maintenance of books and records, supervision of customer accounts, transmittal of funds between customers and third parties, and validation of customer address changes.
Ensure the inspector does not supervise the location and is not supervised by anyone at it, as Rule 3110(c)(3) requires.
Issue a written report per location with findings, owners and due dates.
checklist.done: every location is inspected within its cycle by an independent inspector, with a written report naming findings, owners and due dates.

checklist.step: Execute the Rule 3120 risk-based testing plan
actions: Build the annual testing plan by ranking the high-risk areas — variable annuity sales practice, communications, anti-money laundering, Regulation Best Interest, outside business activities and private securities transactions.
Test each area independently of the business line, sampling transactions and re-performing the supervisory step rather than confirming it was ticked.
Document scope, sample, method, findings and conclusion per area in a workpaper.
Track each finding to closure with an owner and a due date rather than closing on management assurance alone.
checklist.done: each high-risk area has an independent test with documented scope, sample, findings and a tracked remediation item.

checklist.step: Handle complaints as supervisory intelligence, not correspondence
actions: Log every written customer grievance in the Rule 4513 complaint register with the customer name, account, producer, product, allegation, receipt date and disposition.
Route every complaint alleging unsuitable recommendation, misrepresentation of guarantees or unauthorised transaction to Compliance the day it arrives.
Assess each complaint for Rule 4530(a) reportability, and compile the quarterly statistics for filing by the 15th day of the month following quarter end.
Feed the complaint themes by producer and by product into the exception report calibration.
checklist.done: every complaint is registered, routed, assessed for 4530 reportability and reflected in the quarterly statistics filing.

checklist.step: Investigate potential Rule 2020 conduct without delay
actions: Open an investigation on any indication of manipulative, deceptive or fraudulent conduct — forged signatures, altered applications, undisclosed third-party funds movement, or misrepresented guarantees.
Preserve the evidence immediately: email, recorded calls, application images and system audit trails, with a documented hold.
Interview the producer with Compliance present and record the account given, and interview affected customers independently.
Report findings to the Head of Compliance and Regulatory Counsel within the investigation deadline set at opening.
checklist.done: each suspected Rule 2020 matter has preserved evidence, recorded interviews and a reported finding within its deadline.

checklist.step: Apply and record disciplinary action
actions: Apply the discipline ladder consistently: coaching, written warning, heightened supervision plan, production restriction, or termination.
For heightened supervision, write the plan naming the supervisor, the review frequency, the transactions requiring pre-approval and the review end date.
Assess every action for Form U4 disclosure and Rule 4530 reporting, and file within the applicable window.
Record the action, its rationale and its dates on the producer's file.
checklist.done: each disciplinary action has a written rationale, a supervision plan where applicable, and an assessed disclosure and reporting outcome.

checklist.step: Track every finding to closure
actions: Load every inspection finding, testing finding and examination finding into the remediation tracker with an owner, a due date and the control it repairs.
Require evidence of the fix — the amended WSP version, the new exception report, the retrained population — before a finding is closed.
Report overdue findings by owner monthly to the Head of Compliance and by exception to the Compliance Committee.
Re-test closed findings in the next cycle rather than accepting closure on assertion.
checklist.done: no finding closes without evidence of the fix, and overdue findings are reported monthly by owner.

checklist.step: Produce the Rule 3120 annual report of the supervisory control system
actions: Summarise the year's testing, the significant identified exceptions and the additional or amended supervisory procedures created in response.

Include the specific Rule 3120(b) content where the firm's revenue threshold requires it: trends in customer complaints, internal investigations, and any changes to supervisory procedures for the enumerated areas.
Submit the report to senior management at least annually and record the submission date and recipients.
Carry unresolved items forward as open matters rather than closing the report over them.
checklist.done: a dated Rule 3120 report reaches senior management summarising testing, exceptions and procedural changes.

checklist.step: Support the Rule 3130 chief executive certification
actions: Prepare the report evidencing the firm's processes to establish, maintain, review, test and modify compliance policies and written supervisory procedures.
Hold and minute at least one meeting with the Chief Executive Officer in the twelve months before the certification, covering the report's contents and the open issues.
Have the chief executive execute the annual certification and record its date.
File the certification and the supporting report together.
checklist.done: the certification is executed annually with a minuted pre-certification meeting and its supporting report on file.

checklist.step: Report supervisory results into governance
actions: Take the quarterly supervision pack — seven-business-day review timeliness, alert disposition timeliness, inspection coverage, complaint themes and open findings — to the Risk Committee.
Escalate any branch or producer with repeat findings as a named risk rather than an aggregate statistic.
Give the Corporate Secretary the summary for the board pack and confirm the minute records the committee's acceptance.
Carry unresolved items on the committee's open-items schedule.
checklist.done: the quarterly supervision pack is presented and minuted, with repeat-offender branches and producers named.

checklist.step: Archive the supervisory evidence
actions: Archive principal review records, alert cases, inspection reports, testing workpapers, disciplinary files and the Rule 3120 and 3130 documents under FINRA/supervision/<year>.
Apply the six-year SEA Rule 17a-4(b) label to supervisory records and the four-year Rule 4513 label to complaint files.
Confirm retrieval by producer CRD number, branch code, contract number and date.
Record the archive reference on the GRC records.
checklist.done: supervisory records are archived under the correct retention labels and retrievable by producer, branch and contract.

testing.step: Build the transaction and alert population for the quarter
actions: Extract every deferred variable annuity application, exchange, rider election and additional purchase payment with its OSJ receipt date, transmittal date and producer.
Extract every exception alert generated in the period with its rule, generation date and current status.
Extract the branch list with last inspection dates and the complaint register for the same period.
testing.done: the population covers transactions, alerts, branches and complaints with a recorded extract date and counts.

testing.step: Reconcile the transaction population to the issuer and commission records
actions: Reconcile the application extract to the issuer's accepted-business file and to the commission payment file for the same period.
Investigate any contract that paid commission but appears in no application record — business transmitted outside the supervisory queue is the highest-risk gap.
Resolve every difference in writing with the Distribution Operations Manager before sampling.
testing.done: the transaction population reconciles to issuer and commission records with all differences explained in writing.

testing.step: Recompute the Rule 2330 seven-business-day clock across the whole population
actions: For every application recompute the review due date as OSJ receipt date plus seven business days using the exchange holiday calendar.
Compare to the recorded principal decision timestamp and list every review completed on business day 8 or later with its day count.
Challenge any OSJ receipt date later than the customer signature date by more than the mail or upload lag, since a shifted receipt date manufactures timeliness.
List any application transmitted to the issuer before the principal decision as a reportable breach.
testing.done: the seven-business-day clock is recomputed for every application and each late or pre-transmittal case is listed.

testing.step: Draw the sample and document the method
actions: Take 100% of exchanges, 100% of contracts sold to customers over 75, and 100% of transactions by producers under heightened supervision.
Take 25 further transactions by seeded random selection weighted to the highest-volume branches.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering exchanges, senior customers and heightened-supervision producers is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the principal suitability judgement
actions: For each sampled transaction, read the investment profile and the contract terms and reach your own Rule 2330 and Rule 2111 conclusion before opening the principal's review note.
Test the exchange arithmetic yourself: surrender charge incurred, new surrender period, change in total annual charges and benefits lost.
Compare your conclusion to the principal's and record every difference, including approvals with no recorded reasoning.
Screenshot the review record and the profile into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled transaction has an independent suitability conclusion recorded against the principal's.

testing.step: Test alert generation, thresholds and disposition timeliness
actions: Re-run two exception rules yourself against the raw transaction extract and compare your hit list to the alerts the system generated — under-generation is invisible in the alert log.
Obtain the documented threshold for each rule and the date it was last calibrated, and challenge any threshold with no supporting analysis.
For 20 alerts, recompute the disposition day count and confirm each closure records facts, a reason and a named decider.
List any alert closed with a status change and no reasoning as an exception.
testing.done: alert generation is independently reproduced, thresholds are evidenced, and disposition timeliness and reasoning are tested.

testing.step: Test branch inspection coverage and independence
actions: Recompute each location's inspection due date from its last inspection date — annually for OSJs and supervisory branches, every three years for non-supervisory branches — and list every overdue location.
For five inspection reports confirm the Rule 3110(c)(2) scope areas were each addressed and evidenced, not merely listed.
Confirm the inspector neither supervised the location nor reported to anyone at it, using the organisation chart as at the inspection date.
Confirm findings were tracked to closure with evidence of the fix.
testing.done: inspection due dates are recomputed, scope coverage evidenced, and inspector independence proven for each sampled report.

testing.step: Test complaint handling and the quarterly statistics filing
actions: Reconcile the Rule 4513 complaint register to complaints found in the contact centre logs, correspondence review and the legal matter list — registers under-capture more often than they over-capture.
For 15 complaints confirm the allegation, producer, product, disposition and the Rule 4530 reportability assessment are recorded.
Recompute the quarterly statistics filing due date as the 15th day of the month following quarter end and compare it to the FINRA Gateway submission date.
Confirm complaint themes actually changed an exception threshold or a training module rather than being logged and left.
testing.done: the complaint register reconciles to independent sources and the quarterly statistics filing is verified as on time.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the contract or branch, the supervisory step missed, the day count and the customer exposure.
Assign a root cause — receipt date not stamped, principal capacity, threshold miscalibrated, inspection deferred, finding closed without evidence — and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and, for any pre-transmittal or unauthorised transaction, open the customer remediation and the Rule 4530(b) assessment immediately.
Carry open exceptions into the next quarter's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the seven-business-day review rate, the alert disposition rate and inspection coverage against the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper sections behind each figure.
Have the Internal Auditor, independent of the supervised business line, sign the workpaper as reviewer.
Feed the conclusion into the Rule 3120 annual report and report to the Risk Committee at its next sitting.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the review, disposition and inspection rates, a conclusion and its Rule 3120 reporting reference.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the broker-dealer's FINRA and SEC filing calendar — Schedule A assessments (gross income assessment, trading activity fee, personnel assessment), FOCUS reports, the annual audited report, Form Custody and Rule 4530(f) document filings — with the Financial and Operations Principal signing the financial filings

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — FINRA By-Laws Schedule A Sections 1 to 4 (assessments and fees), Rule 4530(f) (requirement to file copies of certain documents), Rule 2210(c)(3) (advertising filing requirements), and SEA Rule 17a-5(a) and (d) (FOCUS and annual reports), each read from the current FINRA Rulebook and the SEC rule text at filing time

In-scope processes.value: Broker-dealer regulatory reporting: monthly and quarterly FOCUS preparation, the annual audited report, quarterly Form Custody, the annual FINRA assessment report and gross income assessment computation, monthly trading activity fee self-reporting, personnel assessment reconciliation, and event-driven Rule 4530(f) document filings

In-scope systems.value: Revenue and expense figures for the gross income assessment and FOCUS come from the general ledger; filings are submitted through FINRA Gateway eFOCUS and FINRA E-Bill, and assessment invoices are settled from the firm's flex-funding account

Compliance procedure documented.value: Broker-Dealer Regulatory Reporting Procedure — the annual filing calendar, the revenue mapping from GL account to Schedule A gross income category, the trading activity fee computation and exemptions, preparer and reviewer roles, and the escalation path for a missed deadline

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Financial Officer and the Head of Compliance; reviewed annually and on any FINRA Regulatory Notice amending Schedule A rates or the FOCUS form

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual audited report within 60 days of fiscal year end under SEA Rule 17a-5(d); FOCUS Part II or IIA by the 17th business day after each period end; Form Custody within the same quarterly window; the annual FINRA assessment report on the date FINRA's E-Bill notice sets; trading activity fee self-reported and paid monthly by the deadline on the E-Bill statement; Rule 4530(f) copies of complaints, arbitrations and indictments within 10 business days of receipt

Deadline reminders configured.value: The filing calendar raises tasks 15, 7 and 2 business days before each FOCUS, Form Custody and assessment due date, and a 45-day-before-year-end task opens the audit timetable so the 60-day annual report deadline is reachable

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Filed FOCUS and annual reports, assessment computations with their GL tie-out, E-Bill payment confirmations and Rule 4530(f) submissions retained six years, the first two in an easily accessible place, per SEA Rule 17a-4(b)

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any filing made after its deadline, any assessment underpayment identified on reconciliation, and any 4530(f) document filed beyond 10 business days is logged with root cause, owner and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs every amended filing, every assessment true-up and the remediation of any late submission

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every FINRA and SEC filing due in the period — FOCUS reports, annual audited report, Form Custody, assessment reports and payments, trading activity fee submissions — plus every complaint, arbitration and indictment received that triggers Rule 4530(f)

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero late filings and zero unpaid assessments; the gross income assessment must tie to the audited revenue within a nil tolerance after documented Schedule A adjustments; any 4530(f) document filed beyond 10 business days is a fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation runs on a schedule, so testing is quarterly over the quarter's due filings with a full annual re-performance of the gross income assessment computation after the audited report is issued

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must be outside the regulatory reporting team and must not have prepared or reviewed any sampled filing

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly regulatory reporting workpaper (filing calendar coverage, deadline recomputation, assessment re-performance, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under FINRA/reporting

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Filing calendar with submission confirmations, the assessment computation with its general ledger tie-out, E-Bill statements and payment confirmations, and the FOCUS-to-GL reconciliations, producible for a FINRA financial examination within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Reporting Manager answers FINRA financial surveillance queries with the Financial and Operations Principal; Regulatory Counsel clears any response conceding a late filing or a misstatement

checklist.step: Build and publish the annual regulatory filing calendar
actions: List every FINRA and SEC filing the broker-dealer owes for the year with its rule cite, period end, statutory due date, preparer, reviewer and signer.

Include FOCUS Part II or IIA by the 17th business day after each period end, the annual audited report within 60 days of fiscal year end, quarterly Form Custody, the annual assessment report and the monthly trading activity fee submission.
Load each due date into the compliance calendar with tasks at 15, 7 and 2 business days before, assigned by name.
Circulate the calendar to Finance, Compliance and the external auditor and get written acknowledgement of the dates.
checklist.done: a published calendar names every filing, its rule cite, due date, preparer, reviewer and signer, with tasks loaded.

checklist.step: Map the general ledger to the Schedule A gross income categories
actions: Extract the broker-dealer entity's revenue trial balance for the assessment year from the general ledger at account level.

Map each revenue account to its FINRA By-Laws Schedule A Section 2 gross income category — commissions on variable contracts, mutual fund concessions, 12b-1 fees, interest and dividends, and other revenue.
Identify and evidence every permitted exclusion, naming the Schedule A provision that allows it, since unexplained exclusions are the first thing FINRA tests.
Have the Controller confirm the mapping in writing before it is used.
checklist.done: every revenue account maps to a named Schedule A category or a cited exclusion, confirmed in writing by the Controller.

checklist.step: Compute the gross income assessment
actions: Apply the current Schedule A Section 2 rate tiers to the mapped gross revenue, showing each tier's base, rate and extension so the arithmetic is inspectable.
Apply the minimum assessment where the computed figure falls below it, and record which applied.
Tie the total mapped revenue to the audited revenue in the annual report, and document every reconciling item line by line.
Have a second preparer re-perform the computation independently before it leaves Finance.
checklist.done: the assessment computation shows tier-by-tier arithmetic, ties to audited revenue with explained reconciling items, and is independently re-performed.

checklist.step: Compute and self-report the trading activity fee monthly
actions: Extract the month's covered sale transactions in equities, options and covered debt from the clearing firm activity file.
Apply the current Schedule A Section 1 per-share and per-contract rates and the per-transaction caps, and identify exempt transactions with the exemption cited.
Reconcile the transaction count to the clearing firm statement before submitting, since the clearing file is the record FINRA will test against.
Self-report and pay through FINRA E-Bill by the deadline on the statement, and file the confirmation.
checklist.done: the monthly trading activity fee is computed from the reconciled clearing file, self-reported and paid on time with the confirmation filed.

checklist.step: Reconcile the personnel assessment to the registered headcount
actions: Take FINRA's personnel assessment invoice from E-Bill and compare the billed registered representative and principal counts to the CRD roster on the assessment date.
Investigate every difference by name — persons terminated but not U5'd still attract the assessment, which makes the difference a registration hygiene finding as well as a billing one.
Where the count is wrong, raise the query with FINRA before payment and record the reference and the resolution.
Pay the assessment by the invoice due date from the flex-funding account and file the confirmation.
checklist.done: the personnel assessment count reconciles by name to the CRD roster, differences are queried, and payment is confirmed.

checklist.step: File the annual FINRA assessment report
actions: In FINRA Gateway open E-Bill and the annual assessment reporting form and enter the gross income figures by Schedule A category from the approved computation.
Attach or reference the audited financial statements supporting the revenue figures.
Have the Financial and Operations Principal review the submission against the computation and sign it before it goes.
Submit by the deadline stated on the FINRA notice and record the confirmation reference on the filing calendar.
checklist.done: the annual assessment report is filed by its deadline, signed by the Financial and Operations Principal, with the confirmation recorded.

checklist.step: Fund the flex-funding account so no payment fails
actions: Forecast the year's FINRA charges — assessments, registration and renewal fees, filing fees and advertising filing fees — and hold a buffer above the peak month.
Monitor the flex-funding balance weekly during the November and December renewal period when the largest draw falls.
Fund by ACH at least three business days before each due date, since a failed payment leaves registrations and filings unpaid on the due date.
Reconcile E-Bill statements to the bank and to the general ledger monthly.
checklist.done: the flex-funding account is funded ahead of every due date and reconciled monthly to the bank and the ledger.

checklist.step: Prepare and file the FOCUS report
actions: Build the FOCUS Part II or IIA from the general ledger at period end, computing net capital, aggregate indebtedness and the minimum net capital requirement.
Reconcile every FOCUS line to the trial balance and document each non-allowable asset and haircut applied.
Have the Financial and Operations Principal review and sign the report before submission.
Submit through FINRA Gateway eFOCUS by the 17th business day after period end and record the confirmation.
checklist.done: the FOCUS report ties line by line to the trial balance, is signed by the Financial and Operations Principal, and is filed by the 17th business day.

checklist.step: Run the annual audit to hit the 60-day report deadline
actions: Agree the audit timetable with the PCAOB-registered auditor at least 45 days before fiscal year end, working back from the SEA Rule 17a-5(d) 60-day filing deadline.
Deliver the prepared-by-client schedules, the net capital computation and the supplemental reports on the agreed dates.
Obtain the auditor's compliance or exemption report as applicable to the firm's carrying status.
Escalate any timetable slippage to the Chief Financial Officer the week it occurs, not in month two.
checklist.done: the audit timetable is agreed and delivered against, with slippage escalated in the week it arises.

checklist.step: File the annual audited report and Form Custody
actions: Assemble the annual report package: audited statement of financial condition, supporting schedules, the net capital computation, the compliance or exemption report and the auditor's reports.
File with the SEC and FINRA within 60 days of fiscal year end and record the exact filing date against the recomputed deadline.
File Form Custody for each quarter within its window and confirm the answers match the firm's actual custody and possession-or-control position.
Distribute the statement of financial condition to customers where required and retain the distribution evidence.
checklist.done: the annual report is filed within 60 days of year end and each Form Custody is filed within its quarterly window.

checklist.step: File Rule 4530(f) copies within 10 business days
actions: Take from Litigation Counsel and the Complaints Manager every civil complaint, arbitration claim or criminal indictment served on the firm or an associated person.
File the copy through FINRA Gateway Rule 4530 Reporting within 10 business days of the firm's receipt, recording the service date and the filing date.
Recompute the day count on the register at filing so lateness is visible immediately rather than at test time.
Confirm nothing is held back pending a legal strategy decision — the filing obligation is independent of the defence.
checklist.done: every 4530(f) document is filed within 10 business days with service date, filing date and day count on the register.

checklist.step: File advertising submissions on the Rule 2210(c)(3) schedule
actions: Take the approved retail communications concerning variable insurance products from the communications register with their first-use dates.
File each with FINRA Advertising Regulation within 10 business days of first use and pay the filing fee from the flex-funding account.
Record the filing reference against the asset and reconcile the filed count to the approved-and-used count monthly.
Escalate any unfiled item at business day 9.
checklist.done: every filable communication is filed within 10 business days and the filed count reconciles to the used count monthly.

checklist.step: Review and sign every filing before submission
actions: Review the FOCUS, annual report and assessment submissions against the supporting computations and the prior period for unexplained movement.
Challenge any figure that moved more than the agreed variance threshold without a written explanation on the file.
Sign the filings within your authority and record the review date, since an unsigned or unreviewed filing is a control failure regardless of accuracy.
Confirm the Financial and Operations Principal has signed the filings that require their capacity.
checklist.done: every filing carries a dated review and the correct signatures, with variances explained in writing.

checklist.step: Handle amendments and late filings openly
actions: Where an error is found after submission, prepare the amended filing immediately and state the nature of the correction rather than resubmitting silently.
Notify FINRA's assigned Risk Monitoring Analyst of any material correction or late filing before they discover it.
Log the event as a compliance exception with the root cause and the process change that prevents recurrence.
Assess whether the error meets the Rule 4530(b) self-reporting standard and start that clock if it does.
checklist.done: every correction is amended, notified to the Risk Monitoring Analyst and assessed against Rule 4530(b).

checklist.step: Archive the filings and their support
actions: Archive per filing the submitted document, its supporting computation and tie-out, the reviewer and signer record and the confirmation reference under FINRA/reporting/<year>/<filing>.
Apply the six-year SEA Rule 17a-4(b) retention label with the first two years easily accessible.
Confirm retrieval by filing type, period end and confirmation reference.
Record the archive reference on the filing calendar row so the calendar doubles as the index.
checklist.done: each filing and its support is archived under six-year retention and retrievable from the filing calendar row.

testing.step: Build the population of filings due in the period
actions: Derive the expected filing list from the rules themselves — SEA Rule 17a-5, FINRA Schedule A, Rule 4530(f) and Rule 2210(c)(3) — rather than from the firm's calendar, so an omitted filing is detectable.
Add the complaint, arbitration and indictment log from Litigation Counsel and the first-use communications register for the 10-business-day filings.
Record the expected count and the source of each expectation.
testing.done: an independently derived list of filings due in the period exists with the rule basis stated for each.

testing.step: Reconcile the expected list to submissions and to E-Bill
actions: Match each expected filing to a FINRA Gateway or SEC submission confirmation and list any expectation with no submission.
Reconcile every E-Bill invoice and payment in the period to the firm's flex-funding account statements and to the general ledger.
Investigate any E-Bill charge with no corresponding internal record, which usually reveals a filing or registration nobody is tracking.
Agree the reconciliation with the Regulatory Reporting Manager before sampling.
testing.done: every expected filing matches a submission confirmation and E-Bill activity reconciles to the ledger, with breaks explained.

testing.step: Recompute every filing deadline from its rule
actions: Recompute the annual report deadline as fiscal year end plus 60 days and compare to the actual filing date.
Recompute each FOCUS deadline as period end plus 17 business days using the exchange holiday calendar.
Recompute the 4530(f) deadlines as service date plus 10 business days and the advertising deadlines as first-use date plus 10 business days.
List every filing made after its recomputed deadline with the day count and the reason recorded on the file.
testing.done: every deadline is recomputed from the rule and each late filing is listed with its day count.

testing.step: Re-perform the gross income assessment computation
actions: Take the audited revenue from the annual report and rebuild the Schedule A category mapping yourself from the account-level trial balance.
Apply the current Schedule A Section 2 rate tiers independently and compare your total to the figure reported to FINRA.
Test every exclusion the firm applied against the Schedule A text and challenge any exclusion supported only by past practice.
Reconcile the reported figure to audited revenue and confirm every reconciling item is separately evidenced.
testing.done: the assessment is independently recomputed and reconciled to audited revenue with every exclusion tested against Schedule A.

testing.step: Test the trading activity fee against the clearing records
actions: For three months, take the clearing firm activity file and recompute the covered sale counts and the fee using the current rates and caps.
Compare to the amounts self-reported through E-Bill and list any under-reporting with the value.
Test the exempt transactions to confirm each exemption is named and supportable rather than assumed.
Confirm payment cleared by the statement deadline in each month tested.
testing.done: three months of trading activity fee are recomputed from clearing records with under-reporting quantified.

testing.step: Test the personnel assessment against CRD headcount
actions: Take the CRD roster as at the assessment date and count registered representatives and principals independently.
Compare to the counts FINRA billed and investigate every difference by name.
Confirm any query raised with FINRA has a reference and a documented resolution rather than an unpaid balance.
Flag differences caused by late Form U5 filings as a registration finding as well as a billing one.
testing.done: the billed personnel counts reconcile by name to CRD, with every difference resolved or logged.

testing.step: Trace FOCUS lines back to the ledger on a sample
actions: Select one FOCUS report and trace net capital, aggregate indebtedness and five material balance lines back to the trial balance.
Re-perform the non-allowable asset deductions and the haircuts and compare to the reported net capital.
Confirm the computed net capital exceeded the minimum requirement on every day of the period tested, not only at period end.
Confirm the Financial and Operations Principal's signature and review date pre-date submission.
testing.done: the sampled FOCUS traces to the ledger, net capital is re-performed, and the signature pre-dates submission.

testing.step: Draw and test the 4530(f) and advertising filing sample
actions: Take 100% of complaints, arbitrations and indictments received in the period and 20 filable communications by seeded random selection.
For each, open the FINRA Gateway submission and match the document filed to the document received, confirming nothing was redacted or substituted.
Recompute each 10-business-day window from the service or first-use date evidenced in the source system rather than the register.
Record the seed, population size and selection date.
testing.done: every 4530(f) item and a documented sample of communications are traced to matching submissions inside 10 business days.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the filing, the deadline missed or the amount misstated, and the regulatory exposure.
Assign a root cause — calendar omission, mapping error, clearing file received late, flex-funding shortfall, service date not captured — and a named owner.
Set a remediation date, require the amended filing or true-up payment immediately, and assess Rule 4530(b) self-reporting.
Carry open exceptions into the next quarter's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the on-time filing rate and the assessment accuracy variance against the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper sections behind each figure.
Have the Internal Auditor, who prepared none of the sampled filings, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report to the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the on-time filing rate, the assessment variance, a conclusion and the committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the customer investment profile standard for variable annuity and variable life recommendations — the profile form, the completeness gate at new business, and the profile refresh cycle; the recommending registered representative captures it and the supervising principal tests it

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — FINRA Rule 2111(a) and Supplementary Material .05(b) (customer-specific suitability), Rule 2330(b) (deferred variable annuity suitability information), Rule 4512(a)(1) (customer account information) and SEC Regulation Best Interest Care Obligation, read from the live Rulebook and the SEC adopting release

In-scope processes.value: Pre-recommendation data capture across every variable annuity and variable life sale: profile collection at account opening, profile completeness gate before the recommendation is made, principal verification at submission, profile refresh at each subsequent recommendation, and update on a life event

In-scope systems.value: The investment profile is captured on the customer record in Salesforce FSC and carried to the application; the completed profile and signed forms are stored against the contract in the policy administration platform

Compliance procedure documented.value: Customer Investment Profile Procedure — the eleven Rule 2111(a) profile elements, the additional Rule 2330(b) data points for deferred variable annuities, the mandatory-field gate, the customer-declined-to-provide route and the refresh triggers

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance with the Distribution Operations Manager accountable for the system gate; reviewed annually and on any change to the profile form or the Regulation Best Interest disclosure

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: The profile must be complete before the recommendation is made, not at submission; Form CRS delivered before or at the time of the recommendation; the Rule 4512 account record updated and, where required, sent to the customer for verification within 30 days of account opening and again within 36 months; profile refreshed at every subsequent recommendation

Deadline reminders configured.value: The new business queue blocks submission where any mandatory profile field is empty; a 36-month profile-refresh task opens on each active contract, and a task opens within 5 business days of any recorded life event such as retirement, bereavement or a change of address to a care facility

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Signed profile forms, system-captured profile versions with timestamps, the customer's declined-to-provide acknowledgement and the Form CRS delivery record retained six years from account closure per SEA Rule 17a-4(b) and Rule 4512(c)

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any recommendation made against an incomplete profile, any profile completed after the application date, and any profile field overwritten without a version history is logged with root cause, owner and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every case where a recommendation proceeded on an incomplete profile, including the customer contact made to repair it

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every variable annuity and variable life recommendation resulting in an application, exchange, additional purchase payment or rider election in the quarter, matched to the customer profile version in force on the recommendation date

Pass/fail thresholds.value: 100% of recommendations must have all eleven Rule 2111(a) profile elements captured and dated before the recommendation date; any profile dated after the application signature is a fail; any missing age, liquidity need or risk tolerance is an automatic fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is per recommendation, so the test runs quarterly across the quarter's recommendation population with 100% coverage of customers aged 75 and over and of all exchanges

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not be the recommending representative or the principal who approved any sampled transaction

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly investment profile workpaper (recommendation population, profile completeness testing, date-order recomputation, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under FINRA/2111

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Per-contract profile pack — signed profile form, system profile version with capture timestamps, Form CRS delivery record and the principal's suitability note — producible for a FINRA cycle examination or a customer arbitration within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Head of Compliance answers FINRA suitability requests; Regulatory Counsel handles arbitration document production and clears any statement about a profile that was completed late

checklist.step: Define the profile form against the eleven Rule 2111(a) elements
actions: Build the profile form with one field per Rule 2111(a) element: age, other investments, financial situation and needs, tax status, investment objectives, investment experience, investment time horizon, liquidity needs, risk tolerance, and any other information the customer discloses.

Add the Rule 2330(b) deferred variable annuity data points: whether the customer has a long-term investment objective, whether they would benefit from tax deferral and the death or living benefit, and their intended use of the contract.
Write the field-level definitions so two representatives asking the same question record the same thing — define liquidity need as a dollar amount and a timeframe, not a category.
Have the Head of Compliance approve the form version and record its effective date.
checklist.done: an approved, versioned profile form carries one defined field per Rule 2111(a) and Rule 2330(b) data point.

checklist.step: Configure the system so the profile gates the recommendation
actions: Make every profile element a mandatory field on the customer record and block progression to the product recommendation screen while any is empty.
Stamp each field with its capture timestamp and the user who entered it, and version the record so later edits do not overwrite what was known at recommendation time.
Build the declined-to-provide path as an explicit selection requiring a reason and the customer's acknowledgement, rather than allowing a blank.
Test the gate in the pre-production environment with a deliberately incomplete profile and evidence that submission is blocked.
checklist.done: the system blocks recommendation on any empty profile field, versions every change, and the block is evidenced by a test case.

checklist.step: Collect the profile at the fact-find before discussing any product
actions: Complete the profile with the customer at the fact-find meeting and record the meeting date, since the profile must inform the recommendation rather than justify it.
Capture other investments and financial situation with figures — investable assets, income, existing annuity and life contracts, outstanding debt — not adjectives.
Record liquidity needs as the amount the customer expects to need and by when, and compare it against the contract's surrender charge schedule in the conversation.
Read the recorded profile back to the customer and note their confirmation in the record.
checklist.done: the profile is captured and confirmed with the customer at a dated fact-find, with financial elements recorded as figures.

checklist.step: Deliver Form CRS and the Regulation Best Interest disclosure
actions: Deliver the relationship summary before or at the time of the recommendation and record the delivery date, method and the version delivered.
Deliver the Regulation Best Interest disclosure covering the scope of services, the fees and costs, and the material conflicts including the compensation the representative receives on this contract.
Where delivery is electronic, retain the send record and the customer's access confirmation rather than an assumption of receipt.
File the delivery evidence against the customer record.
checklist.done: Form CRS and the Regulation Best Interest disclosure are delivered on or before the recommendation date with evidence retained.

checklist.step: Test the recommendation against the recorded profile before presenting it
actions: Compare the contract's surrender charge period against the customer's recorded time horizon and liquidity need, and abandon the recommendation where the contract locks money the customer said they need.
Compare the total annual cost — mortality and expense charge, administrative charge, fund expenses and rider fees — against the customer's stated objective and record why the cost is justified.
Check the concentration: the proposed premium as a percentage of the customer's liquid net worth against the firm's threshold.
Write the reasoned basis in the customer record in plain language before the recommendation is made.
checklist.done: a written reasoned basis links the contract's terms and costs to specific recorded profile elements before presentation.

checklist.step: Capture the Rule 4512 customer account record
actions: Record the Rule 4512(a)(1) account information: customer name and residence, whether of legal age, the names of the associated persons responsible for the account, and the signatures of the approving principal.
For an account with a natural person, record the customer's tax identification number, occupation and employer, and whether they are associated with another member firm.
Send the account record to the customer for verification within 30 days of opening where the rule requires, and again within 36 months, retaining the send evidence.
Record the trusted contact person or the customer's declination, as Rule 4512(a)(1)(F) requires.
checklist.done: the Rule 4512 account record is complete, includes a trusted contact or a recorded declination, and verification is sent within 30 days.

checklist.step: Gate the application at submission on profile completeness and date order
actions: Before transmitting, check the profile version in force is complete and its capture timestamp pre-dates the application signature date.
Reject to the representative any case where the profile was completed on or after the application date, and require the customer conversation to be redone rather than the date to be adjusted.
Attach the profile version, the signed forms and the reasoned basis to the contract record so the pack travels with the contract.
Record the rejection reason on cases returned so the pattern by representative is visible.
checklist.done: no application transmits unless a complete profile version pre-dates the application signature, with rejections reasoned.

checklist.step: Verify the profile as the reviewing principal
actions: As part of the Rule 2330(c) principal review, read the profile for internal consistency — a stated aggressive risk tolerance alongside a two-year liquidity need is a contradiction, not a preference.
Test the arithmetic: premium against stated investable assets, and income against the stated ability to fund future purchase payments.
Where the profile does not support the recommendation, decline the transaction and record the reason rather than requesting a profile amendment.
Record the decision, the reasoning and your CRD number on the transaction.
checklist.done: the principal records a reasoned decision testing profile consistency and arithmetic, and declines rather than amends where unsupported.

checklist.step: Handle customers who decline to provide information
actions: Where a customer declines an element, record what was asked, when, and the customer's reason, with their acknowledgement.
Apply the Rule 2111 Supplementary Material .04 position: a missing element does not excuse the recommendation, so assess whether a reasonable basis still exists without it.
Escalate to the Head of Compliance any recommendation proceeding without age, liquidity need or risk tolerance — those three cannot be inferred.
Record the escalation decision on the contract.
checklist.done: each declined element carries a recorded request, reason and acknowledgement, with escalation where a core element is missing.

checklist.step: Refresh the profile at every subsequent recommendation
actions: Before any subsequent recommendation — additional purchase payment, rider election, fund reallocation, exchange — open the existing profile with the customer and confirm or update each element.
Record the review date even where nothing changed, since an unrefreshed profile from four years ago will not support a current recommendation.
Where an element changes, save a new profile version rather than editing the old one so the record shows what was known when.
Attach the refreshed version to the new transaction.
checklist.done: every subsequent recommendation carries a profile version confirmed or updated on or before its recommendation date.

checklist.step: Trigger a profile update on life events
actions: Open a profile update task within 5 business days of any recorded life event: retirement, bereavement, change of address to a care facility, power of attorney registration or a reported change in health.
Contact the customer or their authorised representative and re-take the affected elements, particularly liquidity needs and time horizon.
Flag the account for enhanced review where a senior customer's circumstances suggest diminished capacity, and involve the trusted contact where the customer permits.
Record the contact, the outcome and the new profile version.
checklist.done: every recorded life event produces a customer contact and a new profile version within the task window.

checklist.step: Run completeness surveillance across the book
actions: Run a monthly report of active contracts whose latest profile is older than 36 months or missing any mandatory element.
Rank by contract value and by customer age so the highest-exposure gaps are worked first.
Assign each gap to the servicing representative with a 30-day completion deadline and escalate at day 25.
Report the completeness percentage by branch to the Head of Compliance monthly.
checklist.done: a monthly completeness report drives assigned, deadline-bound remediation and a branch-level percentage reported to Compliance.

checklist.step: Train representatives on what a usable profile looks like
actions: Deliver the profile module using real, anonymised examples of profiles that failed testing — vague liquidity answers, copied risk tolerances, profiles dated after the application.
Assess with scenario questions requiring the learner to identify the missing or contradictory element.
Assign the module to every representative selling variable products and to their supervising principals, and track completion.
Feed persistent failure patterns into the next Firm Element needs analysis.
checklist.done: every variable product representative and principal completes a profile module built on the firm's own failure examples.

checklist.step: Report profile quality into supervisory governance
actions: Report monthly to the supervising principals: profile completeness rate, late-dated profiles, declined elements and remediation ageing, by branch and by representative.
Name representatives with repeat late-dated profiles as a supervisory concern rather than a data quality one.
Feed the year's figures into the Rule 3120 annual report of the supervisory control system.
Record the committee acceptance date.
checklist.done: profile quality metrics reach supervising principals monthly and the year's figures appear in the Rule 3120 report.

checklist.step: Retain the profile pack with the contract
actions: Archive per contract the signed profile form, every system profile version with its timestamps, the Form CRS and Regulation Best Interest delivery evidence, the reasoned basis and the principal's note.
Apply the six-year-from-account-closure retention required by SEA Rule 17a-4(b) and Rule 4512(c).
Confirm retrieval by contract number, customer name and representative CRD number, since arbitration requests arrive by any of the three.
Record the archive reference on the contract record.
checklist.done: each contract's profile pack is archived under six-year-from-closure retention and retrievable by contract, customer and representative.

testing.step: Build the recommendation population for the quarter
actions: Extract every variable annuity and variable life application, exchange, additional purchase payment and rider election with its signature date, submission date, customer age and representative.
Add fund reallocations and withdrawal elections where the representative made a recommendation, since those carry the same obligation.
Record the extract date and counts so the population is reproducible.
testing.done: a dated recommendation population covering new business, exchanges and in-force activity exists with recorded counts.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to commissions and the customer relationship system
actions: Reconcile the transaction extract to the commission payment file and to activity records in the customer relationship system.
Investigate any paid transaction with no corresponding recommendation record, which indicates business booked outside the profile gate.
Resolve every difference in writing with the Distribution Operations Manager before sampling.
testing.done: the recommendation population reconciles to commissions and relationship records with all differences explained.

testing.step: Test profile completeness across the whole population
actions: Extract the profile version in force on each transaction's recommendation date and test every Rule 2111(a) element for a non-null, non-default value.
List any transaction missing age, liquidity need or risk tolerance as an automatic fail without sampling.
Test for copied answers — identical free-text liquidity or objective wording across many customers of the same representative indicates template completion, not a fact-find.
testing.done: population-wide completeness is tested per element, with core-element gaps and templated answers listed.

testing.step: Recompute the profile-before-recommendation date order
actions: Compare each profile version's capture timestamp to the application signature date and to the recorded recommendation date.
List every case where the profile timestamp falls on or after the application date as a fail, and every case where the profile was edited after submission.
For refreshed profiles, recompute the age of the version relied on and list anything older than 36 months at the recommendation date.
Show the day counts rather than a pass or fail flag.
testing.done: date order is recomputed for every transaction with day counts shown and late-dated or stale profiles listed.

testing.step: Draw the sample and document the method
actions: Take 100% of transactions for customers aged 75 and over, 100% of exchanges and 100% of transactions by representatives with a prior profile exception.
Take 25 further transactions by seeded random selection across branches.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering senior customers, exchanges and repeat offenders is documented with its seed.

testing.step: Re-perform the reasonable-basis judgement on the sample
actions: For each sampled transaction read the profile and the contract terms and reach your own Rule 2111(a) and Regulation Best Interest conclusion before opening the representative's reasoned basis.
Test the specific conflicts: surrender period against time horizon, total annual cost against objective, premium against liquid net worth.
Compare your conclusion to the recorded one and treat a correct conclusion with no recorded reasoning as an exception.
Capture the profile version and the contract illustration into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled transaction has an independent suitability conclusion recorded against the representative's reasoned basis.

testing.step: Trace the profile to the customer's own evidence
actions: For 10 sampled transactions, trace recorded figures — investable assets, income, existing contracts — to the source the customer provided, such as a statement image, a signed fact-find or the recorded call.
Confirm the signed profile form matches the system version relied on, field by field.
Where the customer confirmed the profile verbally, confirm the call recording exists and covers the elements claimed.
Treat a system figure with no customer-provided source as unsupported.
testing.done: ten sampled profiles are traced field by field to customer-provided evidence with unsupported figures listed.

testing.step: Test disclosure delivery and the Rule 4512 account record
actions: For each sampled transaction confirm Form CRS and the Regulation Best Interest disclosure were delivered on or before the recommendation date, with the version and delivery evidence retained.
Confirm the Rule 4512 record holds the required elements and a trusted contact or a recorded declination.
Recompute the 30-day account verification send and the 36-month re-send against their due dates.
List any account whose verification was never sent.
testing.done: disclosure delivery, trusted contact capture and the 30-day and 36-month verification sends are each verified or listed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception naming the contract, the customer, the missing or late element and the representative.
Assign a root cause — gate bypassed, profile completed post-application, templated answers, refresh never triggered, disclosure not evidenced — and a named owner.
Set a remediation date requiring the customer be re-contacted and the profile rebuilt, and assess whether the transaction itself needs unwinding.
Carry open exceptions into the next quarter's test as mandatory retest rows.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the profile completeness rate, the profile-before-recommendation rate and the disclosure delivery rate against the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — citing the workpaper sections behind each figure.
Have the Compliance Officer, who neither recommended nor approved any sampled transaction, sign the workpaper as independent reviewer.
Report to the Compliance Committee, feed the figures into the Rule 3120 report, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the completeness, date-order and disclosure rates, a conclusion and the committee reporting date.
